> striking the tender heart so that it does not stand firm.

And the saying of Ibn Abi Rabi'a or Jamil: [Kamil]

> So she kissed her mouth, taking hold of its horns (of wine),
> the drinking of the nazif, with the coolness of the water of al-Hashraj.

And according to the reading *yunzifun* with a *kasra* on the *zay*, making it active (*mabniyyan lil-fa'il*), there are two interpretations among the scholars:

The first: that it is from *anzafa al-qawm*, when the time of their *nuzf* (intoxication) has come, and *nuzf* is drunkenness. Its parallel is the saying *ahsada al-zar'u* (the crop has been reaped) when its harvest has come, and *aqtafa al-'inab* (the grapes have been picked) when its picking has come. This view's meaning returns to the first.

The second: that it is from *anzafa al-qawm* when their wine is exhausted. From it is the saying of al-Huta'ia: [Tawil]

> By my life, if you have run out (of wine), or you have sobered up,
> then wretched are you as companions, O family of Abjar.

The majority of scholars hold that wine is najis in its essence, for the reasons we have mentioned. Rabi'a, al-Layth, al-Muzani, the companion of al-Shafi'i, and some of the later scholars of Baghdad and Qarawiyyin disagreed on this, as al-Qurtubi transmitted from them in his *Tafsir*.

They argued for the purity of its essence by saying that the things mentioned with it in the verse, namely the wealth gained by gambling (maysir), wealth gained by games of chance (qimar), altars, and arrows, are not najis in their essence, though their use is forbidden.

The majority answered this by saying that His saying *rijs* requires the najasah (impurity) of the essence in all of them. Whatever is excluded by consensus (ijma') or by an explicit text (nass) is excluded by that, and whatever is not excluded by a text or by consensus is necessarily ruled najis. For the exclusion of some of what the general term (al-'amm) covers by a specifier (mukhassis) from among the specifiers does not nullify the use of the general term as evidence for the remainder, as is established in the principles of jurisprudence (usul al-fiqh). To this the words of the author of *Maraqi al-Su'ud* allude: [Rajaz]

> It is a proof according to the majority, if
> a specifier specifies it, clearly defined.

On this basis, the intoxicant that has become widespread today through its use as perfume, known in the Darija dialect as *al-kulaniya*, is najis, and prayer is not permissible with it. What supports this is that His saying, exalted is He, concerning the intoxicant: *fa-jtanibuhu* (so avoid it), requires absolute avoidance, by which nothing of the intoxicant is to be benefited from, and nothing that is with it in the verse in any way, as al-Qurtubi and others said.

The author of this commentary, may Allah pardon him, says: It is not hidden from any fair-minded person that smearing oneself with the mentioned perfume, taking delight in its scent, finding it pleasant and admiring it, while it is intoxicating, and while Allah explicitly states in His Book that wine is *rijs* with what it contains, then it is not permissible for a Muslim to perfume himself with something of which he hears his Lord say that it is *rijs*, as is clear. What confirms this is that the Prophet (ﷺ) «ordered the pouring out of wine». Had it had another benefit, he would have explained it, just as he explained the permissibility of benefiting from the hides of dead animals, and he would not have ordered it poured out.

Know that what Sa'id ibn al-Haddad al-Qarawi used as evidence for the purity of the essence of wine, namely that the Companions poured it out in the streets of Madinah, and that had it been najis they would not have done so, and the Prophet (ﷺ) would have forbidden them, just as he forbade them from relieving themselves in the roads, has no proof in it. For it does not cover the roads entirely, and it is possible to avoid it, because Madinah was spacious, and wine was not so abundant as to be a river or torrent in the roads covering all of them. It was only poured out in a few places where it is possible to avoid it. This is what al-Qurtubi said, and it is evident.

[p-427] [p-428]

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 95:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram﴾. This noble verse implies, by the indication of its discourse, that is, by the implication of its opposite (mafhum al-mukhalafa), that if they come out of their ihram, it is permissible for them to kill game. This implication is stated explicitly in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿But when you have come out of ihram, then hunt﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 2], meaning: if you wish, as its clarification was already explained at the beginning of this noble surah.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever among you kills it intentionally﴾, to the end of the verse.

(p-429) The majority of scholars (jumhur al-'ulama') held that the meaning of this noble verse, ﴿And whoever among you kills it intentionally﴾, is that it refers to killing it while remembering that it is forbidden. Mujahid, may Allah have mercy on him, differed from the majority, saying: the meaning of the verse, ﴿And whoever among you kills it intentionally﴾, is killing it while he is forgetful of his ihram. He cited as evidence His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever returns, Allah will take retribution from him﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 95], as its clarification will come, Allah willing, exalted is He.

We have already mentioned in the introduction to this book that among the types of clarification (bayan) it contains is that some scholars state an opinion regarding a verse while the verse contains an indicator showing that this opinion is not correct. Knowing this, be aware that in the verse there is a clear indicator showing that Mujahid's opinion is not correct, namely His saying, exalted is He: ﴿so that he may taste the consequence of his action﴾. It indicates that he is intentionally doing something impermissible, whereas the forgetful person is, by consensus, not sinful. Therefore it is not fitting to say of him: ﴿so that he may taste the consequence of his action﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 95], as you see. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 96 (part 1 of 7):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Lawful for you is the game of the sea﴾, the verse.

The apparent generality of this noble verse includes the permissibility of the game of the sea for one in the state of ihram for hajj or ʿumrah, and this is so, as His specification of the prohibition of hunting on land for the muhrim, in His saying: ﴿And the game of the land is forbidden to you as long as you are in the state of ihram﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 96], demonstrates. For it is understood from it that the game of the sea is not forbidden to the muhrim, as is evident.

Issues relating to hunting
During ihram or within the Sacred Precinct (al-Haram)

The first issue: The scholars have agreed on the prohibition of hunting land game for one in the state of ihram for hajj or ʿumrah.

This consensus applies to the land game whose meat is eaten, such as the gazelle, the antelope and the like. It is also forbidden for him to point out the game or to direct someone to it, due to what is established in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Abu Qatadah, may Allah be pleased with him, that he was with a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was not in ihram and they were in ihram, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in ihram in front of them. They saw a wild ass, and Abu Qatadah was busy mending his sandal, so they did not inform him, and they wished that he had seen it. Then he saw it, mounted his horse, and forgot his whip and his spear, so he said to them: "Hand me the whip and the spear." They said: "By Allah, we will not help you in this." So he became angry, dismounted, took them himself, mounted, charged at the wild ass and slaughtered it. Then he brought it, and it had died. They fell upon it, eating it. Then they doubted their eating of it while they were in ihram, so they reached the Prophet ﷺ and asked him, and he confirmed them in eating it. Abu Qatadah had given him a foreleg of the wild ass, and he ﷺ ate from it. In Muslim's version: "Did any of you gesture toward it, or order him to do something?" They said: No. He said: "Then eat it."

In al-Bukhari's version: "Is there any one of you who ordered him to charge at it, or gestured to it?" They said: No. He said: "Then eat what remains of its meat."

The scholars have unanimously agreed that what a muhrim hunts is not lawful to eat for the muhrim who hunted it, nor for another muhrim, nor for a non-muhrim, because it is carrion.

The scholars differed concerning the muhrim eating what a lawful (non-muhrim) person has hunted, in three opinions. It was said: it is not permissible for him to eat it at all. It was said: it is permissible absolutely. It was said: there is a distinction between what was hunted on his behalf and what was hunted not on his behalf, so the first is prohibited and the second is not.

Those of the first opinion argued with the hadith of al-Sab' ibn Jathamah, may Allah be pleased with him: "That he presented to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a wild ass while he was at al-Abwa' or Waddan, and he returned it to him. When he saw what was in his face he said: 'We did not return it to you except that we are in ihram.'" Agreed upon. And in the narration of Ahmad and Muslim: "the meat of a wild ass."

They also argued with the hadith of Zayd ibn Arqam, may Allah be pleased with him: that "a part of the meat of game was presented to the Prophet ﷺ, and he returned it and said: 'We do not eat it, for we are in ihram.'" Narrated by Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i.

They also argued with the generality of the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And the game of the land is forbidden to you as long as you are in the state of ihram﴾. This view is related from ʿAli, Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn ʿUmar, al-Layth, al-Thawri, Ishaq, ʿAisha and others.

Those who said it is permissible for the muhrim to eat what a non-muhrim has hunted, absolutely, argued with the generality of the hadiths reporting the permissibility of the muhrim eating from the game of a non-muhrim, such as the hadith of Talhah ibn ʿUbaydullah in Muslim and in Imam Ahmad: "That he was among a group who were in ihram, and birds were presented to them while Talhah was asleep. Some of them ate and some of them abstained from eating out of scrupulousness. When Talhah awoke, he agreed with those who had eaten and said: 'We ate it with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.'"

And like the hadith of al-Bahzi, whose name is Zayd ibn Ka'b, that he "said to the Prophet ﷺ concerning a wounded wild ass in some part of Wadi al-Rawha, and he was its owner: 'Take charge of this ass.' So the Prophet ﷺ ordered Abu Bakr to divide it among the travellers, and they were in ihram." Narrated by the two Imams Malik in his Muwatta', Ahmad in his Musnad, and al-Nasa'i, and Ibn Khuzaymah and others declared it sound, as Ibn Hajar said. Among those who held its permissibility absolutely were Abu Hanifah and his companions.

The author of this commentary, may Allah pardon him, says: The most apparent of the opinions and the strongest in evidence is the detailed opinion that distinguishes between what is hunted for the sake of the muhrim, which is not lawful for him, and what a lawful person hunts not for the sake of the muhrim, which is lawful for him.

The evidence for this is two matters:

The first: Combining the evidences is obligatory whenever possible, because acting upon both evidences is better than discarding one of them, and there is no way to combine them except this way, and whoever departs from it must discard authentic texts.

The second: Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: "The game of the land is lawful for you while you are in ihram, so long as you do not hunt it or it is not hunted for you." Narrated by Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Khuzaymah, Ibn Hibban, al-Hakim, al-Bayhaqi and al-Daraqutni.

Al-Shafi'i said: This is the finest hadith narrated in this chapter and the most analogous. If it is said regarding the chain of this hadith: ʿAmr ibn Abi ʿAmr, mawla of al-Muttalib ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Hantab, from his mawla al-Muttalib, from Jabir, and ʿAmr is disputed concerning, al-Nasa'i said of him: "He is not strong in hadith," although Malik narrated from him.

And al-Tirmidhi said concerning his mawla al-Muttalib as well: "It is not known that he heard from Jabir." And al-Tirmidhi also said in another place, saying: Muhammad (al-Bukhari) said: "I do not know that he heard from anyone of the Companions, except his saying: 'A man who witnessed the sermon of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ related to me.'"

The answer is that none of this contains anything requiring the rejection of this hadith, because the aforementioned ʿAmr is trustworthy (thiqah), one of the narrators of al-Bukhari and Muslim, and among those from whom Malik ibn Anas narrated. All of this indicates that he is trustworthy. Ibn Hajar said of him in al-Taqrib: "Trustworthy, who may sometimes err." And al-Nawawi said of him in Sharh al-Muhadhdhab: "As for the weakening of ʿAmr ibn Abi ʿAmr, it is not established, because al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated for him in their Sahihs and relied upon him, and they are the exemplars in this field."

(p-432) He was relied upon by Malik, who narrated from him, and he is the exemplar; and it is known of his practice that he does not narrate in his book except from a trustworthy source. Ahmad ibn Hanbal said of him: "There is no harm in him." Abu Zur'ah said: "He is trustworthy." Abu Hatim said: "There is no harm in him."

Ibn ʿAdi said: "There is no harm in him, because Malik narrated from him, and Malik narrates only from one who is truthful and trustworthy." I say: It is known that criticism (jarh) is not established unless it is specified, and Ibn Ma'in and al-Nasa'i did not specify it in a way that establishes the weakening of the aforementioned ʿAmr. The statement of al-Tirmidhi that his mawla al-Muttalib ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Hantab is not known to have heard from Jabir, and the statement of al-Bukhari to al-Tirmidhi: "I do not know that he heard from anyone of the Companions except his saying: 'A man who witnessed the sermon of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ related to me'," contain nothing that requires rejecting his narration, because of what we mentioned in Surat al-Nisa' that the verified position is sufficiency with contemporaneity (al-mu'asarah).

Nor does it necessitate the establishment of meeting (liqa'), let alone the establishment of hearing (sama'), as Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj, may Allah have mercy on him, clarified in the introduction to his Sahih, in a manner beyond which there is nothing further. Moreover, al-Bukhari mentioned in this statement which al-Tirmidhi quoted from him that al-Muttalib, mawla of ʿAmr ibn Abi ʿAmr mentioned, explicitly stated narration from one who heard the sermon of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and this is an explicit statement of hearing from some of the Companions beyond doubt.

Al-Nawawi said in Sharh al-Muhadhdhab: "As for al-Muttalib's encounter with Jabir, Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'He narrated from Jabir,' and said: 'It is likely that he met him.' This is the statement of Ibn Abi Hatim, so doubt arose regarding his meeting. The school of Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj, who claimed consensus in the introduction to his Sahih, is that meeting is not a condition for the continuity of a hadith; rather, the possibility of it suffices, and possibility is certainly present. The school of ʿAli ibn al-Madini, al-Bukhari and the majority is that the establishment of meeting is a condition. According to Muslim's school the hadith is continuous (muttasil), and according to the majority's school it is mursal of one of the senior Successors, and it has already been stated that the mursal of a senior Successor is held as evidence by us when reinforced by the statement of the Companions, or the statement of most scholars, or other matters previously mentioned.

This hadith has been reinforced, and among the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, those who held it will be mentioned in the section on the positions of the scholars." End of al-Nawawi's words. Thus the soundness of using the aforementioned hadith as evidence became apparent under every assumption, according to the schools of the four Imams, because al-Shafi'i, among them, is the one who does not use the mursal as evidence (p-433), and you have learned his use of this hadith on the assumption of its being mursal.

The author of this commentary, may Allah pardon him, says: Yes, it is required for the acceptance of the narration of a mudallis that he explicitly state hearing, and the aforementioned al-Muttalib is a mudallis. However, the well-known position of the school of Malik, Abu Hanifah and Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on them, is the soundness of using the mursal as evidence, especially when it is reinforced by other evidence as here, and you have learned from al-Nawawi's statement the agreement of the Shafi'is.

Those who held that the mursal is a proof argued that a trustworthy narrator does not omit the intermediary while firmly attributing the hadith to one above it unless he is certain of the uprightness and trustworthiness of the one he omitted. Some Malikis said: the mursal takes precedence over the musnad, because he who omits the intermediary in a mursal has guaranteed the uprightness and trustworthiness of what he omitted, unlike the musnad, which refers the examiner to it and does not guarantee for him uprightness and trustworthiness. The author of Maraqi al-Su'ud alluded to this in his section on the mursal, saying:

"It is a proof, but it is preferred over the musnad, and the reverse has been declared sound."

It is well known that whoever uses the mursal as evidence also uses the 'an'anah of a mudallis, all the more so. Thus the soundness of using the aforementioned hadith is established according to Malik, Abu Hanifah and Ahmad. Moreover, this hadith has a supporting narration with al-Khatib and Ibn ʿAdi, from the narration of ʿUthman ibn Khalid al-Makhzumi, from Malik, from Ibn ʿUmar, as Ibn Hajar transmitted in al-Talkhis and others, and it strengthens it.

Even if this ʿUthman is weak, because a weak narration strengthens a mursal, as is known in the sciences of hadith. Thus it is apparent that this hadith of Jabir is sound, and that it is explicit on the point under dispute. It also combines these evidences in the same manner of combination we mentioned at first. It has thus become clear that the hadiths indicating the prohibition for the muhrim to eat what a lawful person hunted are all understood as referring to the case where it was hunted on his behalf, and that the hadiths indicating the permissibility of eating from it are understood as referring to the case where it was not hunted on his behalf. And if it were hunted on behalf of a specific muhrim, it would be forbidden to all the muhrims, contrary to those who said it is forbidden only to that specific muhrim for whom it was hunted.

This is related from ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan, may Allah be pleased with him, and it is the apparent meaning of his saying ﷺ: "or it is hunted for you." The first position is indicated by the apparent meaning of his saying in the hadith of Abu Qatadah: "Is there any one of you who ordered him to charge at it, or gestured to it?" They said: No. He said: "Then eat it." Its implication is that the gesture of one of them makes it forbidden to all of them. It is also supported by what Abu Dawud related from ʿAli, that he was invited while in ihram to a meal on which was game, and he said: "Feed it to someone lawful, for we are in ihram." This is the well-known position of Malik among his companions, along with the variation of his statements on this matter.

* *

**Issue two:** Hunting game by slaughter is not permitted for one in ihram (the state of pilgrim consecration). If he slaughters it, it is carrion (maytah) and no one may eat it, whoever he is, because there is no difference between killing it by wounding and killing it by slaughter. This is based on the general wording of Allah's words: ﴿Do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 95]. This is the view of Malik and his companions, as al-Qurtubi and others have reported from them. It is also the view of al-Hasan, al-Qasim, Salim, al-Awza'i, Ishaq, the Companions of Opinion (Ahl al-Ra'y, the Hanafis), and al-Shafi'i in one of his two opinions. Al-Hakam, al-Thawri and Abu Thawr said: there is no harm in eating it. Ibn al-Mundhir said: it is in the same position as the slaughtered animal of a thief.

'Amr ibn Dinar and Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani said: it may be eaten by one who is not in ihram. This is one of al-Shafi'i's two opinions, as Ibn Qudamah reported from them in *al-Mughni* and elsewhere.

Those who held this view argued that whoever's slaughter is valid for animals other than game, his slaughter of game is valid, just as for a non-pilgrim. The correct view, however, is what has preceded: the slaughter by one in ihram does not make the game lawful, and it is not considered a valid slaughter for it, because killing game is forbidden to him. Moreover, his slaughter does not make it lawful for him to eat it, by consensus (ijma'). If the slaughter does not make it lawful for the slaughterer, it is all the more fitting that it not make it lawful for others, because the derivative follows the source in its rulings, so it is not valid for what does not hold for its source. This was stated by al-Qurtubi, and it is clear.

* *

**Issue three:** Land animals are of three kinds. One kind is game by consensus, which is any wild animal whose meat is lawful to eat, such as the gazelle. Killing it is prohibited for one in ihram, and if he kills it he owes a compensation (jaza'). A second kind is not game by consensus, and there is no harm in killing it. A third kind is disputed.

As for the kind that may be killed and is not game by consensus, it is: the crow, the kite, the scorpion, the mouse and the rabid dog.

As for the disputed kind, it includes the lion, the panther, the leopard and the wolf. Al-Bukhari and Muslim, in their two *Sahihs*, related from 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) that she said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded the killing of five wicked creatures (fawasiq) both within the sanctuary and outside it: the crow, the kite, the scorpion, the mouse and the rabid dog."

Also in the two *Sahihs*, from Ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Five of the creatures there is no sin upon the muhrim for killing them," and then he listed the five mentioned above. There is no doubt that the snake is more deserving of being killed than the scorpion.

Muslim also related from Ibn Mas'ud that "the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded a muhrim to kill a snake at Mina." And from Ibn 'Amr, who was asked: "What may a man kill of creatures while he is in ihram?" He said: "One of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) told me that he used to command the killing of the rabid dog, the mouse, the scorpion, the kite, the crow and the snake." Muslim also related this.

The hadiths on this topic are many. The established principle in the sources of law (usul) is to restrict the general term "crow" to the white-patched crow (al-abqa'), which has white on it, on the basis of what Muslim related from the hadith of 'A'ishah in counting the five wicked creatures, which mentions "the white-patched crow." It is established in the usul that the unrestricted (mutlaq) is to be read in light of the restricted (muqayyad). As for what some scholars answered, that the reports of "the crow" without qualification are agreed upon and therefore more authentic than the report restricting it to the white-patched crow, this does not stand, because there is no contradiction between a restricted and an unrestricted text. The restriction is an explanation of what is meant by the unrestricted.

No attention is to be paid to the view of 'Ata' and Mujahid that the muhrim may not kill the crow, because it contradicts the explicit and authentic text and the view of the majority of scholars. Nor is any attention to be paid to the view of Ibrahim al-Nakha'i that killing the mouse requires a compensation, for it likewise contradicts the text and the view of most scholars. Nor is any attention to be paid to the view of al-Hakam and Hammad: "The muhrim should not kill the scorpion or the snake." Undoubtedly, predatory beasts such as the lion, the panther and the leopard are more deserving of being killed than the dog, because they are stronger in wounding and more violent in their attack.

Know that the scholars differed over what is meant by the rabid dog (al-kalb al-'aqur). Sa'id ibn Mansur reported from Abu Hurayrah, with a good chain (isnad), that it means the lion. Ibn Hajar said this. And from Zayd ibn Aslam, he said: "What dog is more wounding than the snake?"

Zufar said: what is meant here is the wolf alone. Malik said in the *Muwatta'*: "Whatever wounds people, attacks them and frightens them, such as the lion, the panther, the leopard and the wolf, is 'aqur (rabid)." Abu 'Ubayd related the same from Sufyan, and this is the view of the majority.

Abu Hanifah said: what is meant here by the dog is specifically the dog as it is commonly known, and nothing else is attached to it in this ruling except the wolf. The majority argued with Allah's words: ﴿And what you have taught of the trained hunting animals, training them as dogs are trained﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 4], deriving the term from the name "dog" (kalb). They also argued with the Prophet's (ﷺ) words about the son of Abu Lahab: "O Allah, set upon him one of Your dogs," and then the lion killed him. This was related by al-Hakim and others with a good chain.

The author of this commentary (may Allah pardon him) says: The verified position is that predatory beasts are not game, so it is permissible to kill them for the muhrim and for others, both within the sanctuary and outside it. This is because, as is established in the usul, the cause (illah) generalizes its effect (ma'lul). Since his words "'aqur" (wounding) are the cause for killing the dog, it is known from this that every animal whose nature is to wound is likewise.

For this reason, the scholars did not differ that his (ﷺ) words in the hadith of Abu Bakrah, which is agreed upon: "No judge should judge between two persons while he is angry," indicate that this cause, which in the apparent meaning of the hadith is anger, generalizes its effect. So it is forbidden for a judge to rule while he is in any state that disturbs the mind and prevents him from fully examining the matters, whatever it is, whether anger or something else, such as excessive hunger or thirst, excessive sadness or joy, or needing to urinate or defecate, and the like.

To this point the author of *Marāqī al-Su'ūd* alluded in his statement on the topic of the cause, in the meter (rajaz):

"It may be restricted and it may be generalized according to its origin, but it is not broken."

This is supported by what Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and Imam Ahmad related from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: that the Prophet (ﷺ) "was asked about what the muhrim may kill, and he said: 'The snake, the scorpion, the fuwaysiqah (the mouse), he may shoot at the crow but not kill it, the rabid dog, the kite, and the predatory beast (al-sab' al-'adiy).'" Al-Tirmidhi graded this hadith as good (hasan).

Ibn Kathir weakened the narration of Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad. Ibn Hajar said in *al-Talkhis*: "In it is Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad, who is weak, and in it is an objectionable wording, which is his saying: 'He may shoot at the crow but not kill it.'" Al-Nawawi said in *Sharh al-Muhadhdhab*: "If this report is authentic, his statement is understood to mean that the recommendation to kill the crow is not as emphasized as the recommendation to kill the snake and others."

The author of this commentary (may Allah pardon him) says: The weakening of this hadith and the refusal to use it as evidence is open to objection on two grounds:

The first: it is on the condition of Muslim, because Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad is among the narrators of his *Sahih*, and al-Bukhari cited him in suspended form (ta'liq). Refusing to use a hadith that meets the condition of Muslim is not free from scrutiny. Muslim mentioned in the introduction to his *Sahih* that whoever's narrations he included outside of corroborations and supporting chains, the least of their status is that the report is accepted. Thus Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad is, in Muslim's work, one whose report is accepted. To this alludes the statement of al-'Iraqi in his *Alfiyyah*:

"He needed to descend in the chain to Yazid ibn Abi Ziyad."

The second: even if we assume this hadith to be weak, it is strengthened by what is established in the agreed-upon hadiths about the permissibility of killing the rabid dog both in ihram and within the sanctuary. The predatory beast either enters into what is meant by it, or it is attached to it by a sound analogy about which there is no dispute. As for what Imam Abu Hanifah (may Allah have mercy on him) mentioned, that only the wolf is attached to the rabid dog because it resembles it more than others, this is not evident, because there is no doubt that the violence of the lion and the panther, for example, is greater than the wounding of the dog and the wolf. It is not clear that killing a weaker harm should be permitted while killing a stronger one is prohibited, because in the latter there is the cause of the ruling and something more. This type of attachment is, according to most scholars of usul, from the implication of the wording (dalalat al-lafz), not from qiyas (analogy), contrary to al-Shafi'i and a group, as we have mentioned in the chapter of *al-Nisa'*.

Al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir of this verse, and his words are: "I say: It is strange that Abu Hanifah (may Allah have mercy on him) treats wheat as analogous to barley (wheat being subject to the same ruling of measure) by the cause of measuring by volume, but does not treat predatory beasts as analogous to the dog by the cause of wickedness and wounding, as Malik and al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on them both) did."

Know that the game, according to al-Shafi'i, is only that whose meat is lawful to eat. So for him there is nothing due for killing what is not eaten, and the young and the adult of it are the same for him. The exception is the offspring of a lawful-to-eat animal and an unlawful one, which he holds may not be hunted, even though its meat is unlawful to eat, such as the *sim'* (hybrid of wolf and hyena). He said: There is nothing due for the *rakhamah* (vulture), the beetles, the lice, the ticks, or whatever is not eaten, because these are not game, as Allah says: ﴿And the game of the land is forbidden to you as long as you are in ihram﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 96]. This indicates that the game forbidden to them is that which was lawful for them before ihram. This is the position of Imam Ahmad.

As for Malik (may Allah have mercy on him), he held that whatever does not attack among the predators, such as the domestic cat, the fox, the hyena and what resembles them, may not be killed. If one kills it, he must compensate. He said: "I do not think the muhrim should kill the cubs of wolves. If he kills them, he must compensate, and they are like the chicks of crows."

The author of this commentary (may Allah pardon him) says: As for the hyena, it is not like what was mentioned with it, because a text has been revealed about it specifically, not about the others: it is game for which compensation is required, as will come, Allah willing.

Malik did not permit the muhrim to kill the wasp, and likewise the ant, the fly and the flea. He said: "If a muhrim kills one of them, he should feed something." But it is established from 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) that killing the wasp is permitted. Some scholars likened it to the scorpion, and some said: if it begins the harm, it may be killed, otherwise not. The most analogous of these views is what is established from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, because by its nature it harms.

We have already mentioned from al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and others that there is nothing due for non-game that is eaten, and this is the apparent meaning of the Noble Qur'an.

* *

**Issue four:** The scholars agreed that if a muhrim hunts game forbidden to him, he owes its compensation, as is the explicit meaning of Allah's words: ﴿So its compensation is an equivalent of what he killed of livestock, judged by two just men among you, as an offering reaching the Ka'bah, or an expiation: feeding the needy, or the equivalent of that in fasting, that he may taste the consequence of his affair﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 95].

Know first that what is meant by Allah's words: ﴿And whoever among you kills it intentionally﴾ is that he intends to kill it while remembering his ihram, as is the explicit meaning of the verse. This is also the view of the majority of scholars.

As for what Mujahid explained it to mean, that it means he intends to kill it while forgetting his ihram, citing Allah's words after it: ﴿And whoever returns, Allah will take retribution from him﴾, he said: If he were remembering his ihram, punishment would be due upon him the first time. He also said: If he remembered his ihram, his pilgrimage would be invalid because he committed a prohibited act of ihram. This view is not correct, nor is it apparent, because it contradicts the apparent meaning of the Qur'an without evidence. Furthermore, Allah's words: ﴿That he may taste the consequence of his affair﴾ indicate that he intentionally committed the prohibited act, and one who forgets his ihram has not intentionally committed a prohibited act.

Having known this, know that the one who kills game intentionally, aware of his ihram, owes the compensation mentioned in the verse, by the explicit text of the Noble Qur'an. This is the view of the majority of scholars, contrary to Mujahid. Allah, exalted is He, did not mention in this noble verse the ruling for one who forgets or one who errs.

The difference between them is this: the one who forgets is the one who intends to kill game while forgetting his ihram, and the one who errs is the one who shoots at something other than game, such as if he shoots at a target and thereby kills game without intending to kill it.

وَلا خِلافَ بَيْنِ العُلَماءِ أنَّهُما لا إثْمَ عَلَيْهِما، لِقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكم جُناحٌ فِيما أخْطَأْتُمْ بِهِ﴾ الآيَةَ [الأحزاب: ٥]، ولِما قَدَّمْنا في ”صَحِيحٍ مُسْلِمٍ“: «أنَّ النَّبِيَّ ﷺ لَمّا (p-٤٣٩)قَرَأ: ﴿رَبَّنا لا تُؤاخِذْنا إنْ نَسِينا أوْ أخْطَأْنا﴾ [البقرة: ٢٨٦]، أنَّ اللَّهَ قالَ: قَدْ فَعَلْتُ».

أمّا وُجُوبُ الجَزاءِ عَلَيْهِما فاخْتَلَفَ فِيهِ العُلَماءُ.

فَذَهَبَ جَماعَةٌ مِنَ العُلَماءِ: مِنهُمُ المالِكِيَّةُ، والحَنَفِيَّةُ، والشّافِعِيَّةُ إلى وُجُوبِ الجَزاءِ في الخَطَإ، والنِّسْيانِ؛ لِدَلالَةِ الأدِلَّةِ عَلى أنَّ غُرْمَ المَتْلَفاتِ لا فَرْقَ فِيهِ بَيْنَ العامِدِ وبَيْنَ غَيْرِهِ. وقالُوا: لا مَفْهُومَ مُخالَفَةٍ لِقَوْلِهِ ﴿مُتَعَمِّدًا﴾؛ لِأنَّهُ جَرْيٌ عَلى الغالِبِ، إذِ الغالِبُ ألّا يَقْتُلَ المُحْرِمُ الصَّيْدَ إلّا عامِدًا، وجَرى النَّصُّ عَلى الغالِبِ مِن مَوانِعِ اعْتِبارِ دَلِيلِ خِطابِهِ، أعْنِي مَفْهُومَ مُخالَفَتِهِ (mafhum al-mukhalafa: المفهوم المخالف، أي الحكم المستفاد من نفي الحكم عما خالف المنطوق)، وإلَيْهِ الإشارَةُ بِقَوْلِ صاحِبِ ”مَراقِي السُّعُودِ“ في مَوانِعِ اعْتِبارِ مَفْهُومِ المُخالَفَةِ: [ الرَّجَزُ ]
؎أوْ جَهِلَ الحُكْمَ أوِ النُّطْقُ انْجَلَبْ لِلسُّؤْلِ أوْ جَرى عَلى الَّذِي غَلَبْ

وَلِذا لَمْ يَعْتَبِرْ جُمْهُورُ العُلَماءِ مَفْهُومَ المُخالَفَةِ في قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿اللّاتِي في حُجُورِكُمْ﴾ [النساء: ٢٣]؛ لِجَرْيهِ عَلى الغالِبِ. وقالَ بَعْضُ مَن قالَ بِهَذا القَوْلِ، كالزُّهْرِيِّ: وجَبَ الجَزاءُ في العَمْدِ بِالقُرْآنِ العَظِيمِ، وفي الخَطَإ والنِّسْيانِ بِالسُّنَّةِ. قالَ ابْنُ العَرَبِيِّ: إنْ كانَ يُرِيدُ بِالسُّنَّةِ الآثارَ الَّتِي ورَدَتْ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، وعُمَرَ فَنِعِمّا هي، وما أحْسَنَها أُسْوَةً.

واحْتَجَّ أهْلُ هَذا القَوْلِ: بِأنَّهُ ﷺ «سُئِلَ عَنِ الضَّبُعِ، فَقالَ: ”هي صَيْدٌ“»، وجَعَلَ فِيها إذا أصابَها المُحْرِمُ كَبْشًا، ولَمْ يَقُلْ عَمْدًا ولا خَطَأً، فَدَلَّ عَلى العُمُومِ. وقالَ ابْنُ بُكَيْرٍ مِن عُلَماءِ المالِكِيَّةِ: قَوْلُهُ سُبْحانَهُ: ﴿مُتَعَمِّدًا﴾ لَمْ يُرِدْ بِهِ التَّجاوُزَ عَنِ الخَطَإ، وذِكْرُ التَّعَمُّدِ لِبَيانِ أنَّ الصَّيْدَ لَيْسَ كابْنِ آدَمَ الَّذِي لَيْسَ في قَتْلِهِ عَمْدًا كَفّارَةٌ.

وَقالَ القُرْطُبِيُّ في ”تَفْسِيرِهِ“: إنَّ هَذا القَوْلَ بِوُجُوبِ الجَزاءِ عَلى المُخْطِئِ، والنّاسِي، والعامِدِ، قالَهُ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، ورُوِيَ عَنْ عُمَرَ، وطاوُسٍ، والحَسَنِ، وإبْراهِيمَ، والزُّهْرِيِّ، وبِهِ قالَ مالِكٌ، والشّافِعِيُّ، وأبُو حَنِيفَةَ، وأصْحابُهم.

وَذَهَبَ بَعْضُ العُلَماءِ إلى أنَّ النّاسِيَ، والمُخْطِئَ لا جَزاءَ عَلَيْهِما، وبِهِ قالَ الطَّبَرِيُّ، وأحْمَدُ بْنُ حَنْبَلٍ في إحْدى الرِّوايَتَيْنِ، وسَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ، وأبُو ثَوْرٍ، وهو مَذْهَبُ داوُدَ، ورُوِيَ أيْضًا عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، وطاوُسٍ، كَما نَقَلَهُ عَنْهُمُ القُرْطُبِيُّ.

واحْتَجَّ أهْلُ هَذا القَوْلِ بِأمْرَيْنِ:
(p-٤٤٠)الأوَّلُ: مَفْهُومُ قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَمَن قَتَلَهُ مِنكم مُتَعَمِّدًا﴾ الآيَةَ، فَإنَّهُ يَدُلُّ عَلى أنَّ غَيْرَ المُتَعَمِّدِ لَيْسَ كَذَلِكَ.
الثّانِي: أنَّ الأصْلَ بَراءَةُ الذِّمَّةِ، فَمَنِ ادَّعى شَغْلَها، فَعَلَيْهِ الدَّلِيلُ.
قالَ مُقَيِّدُهُ - عَفا اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: هَذا القَوْلُ قَوِيٌّ جِدًّا مِن جِهَةِ النَّظَرِ والدَّلِيلِ.

* *

المَسْألَةُ الخامِسَةُ: إذا صادَ المُحْرِمُ الصَّيْدَ، فَأكَلَ مِنهُ، فَعَلَيْهِ جَزاءٌ واحِدٌ لِقَتْلِهِ، ولَيْسَ في أكْلِهِ إلّا التَّوْبَةُ والِاسْتِغْفارُ، وهَذا قَوْلُ جُمْهُورِ العُلَماءِ، وهو ظاهِرُ الآيَةِ، خِلافًا لِأبِي حَنِيفَةَ القائِلِ بِأنَّ عَلَيْهِ أيْضًا جَزاءَ ما أكَلَ، يَعْنِي قِيمَتَهُ. قالَ القُرْطُبِيُّ: وخالَفَهُ صاحِباهُ في ذَلِكَ، ويُرْوى مِثْلُ قَوْلِ أبِي حَنِيفَةَ عَنْ عَطاءٍ.

* *

المَسْألَةُ السّادِسَةُ: إذا قَتَلَ المُحْرِمُ الصَّيْدَ مَرَّةً بَعْدَ مَرَّةٍ، حُكِمَ عَلَيْهِ بِالجَزاءِ في كُلِّ مَرَّةٍ، في قَوْلِ جُمْهُورِ العُلَماءِ مِنهم مالِكٌ، والشّافِعِيُّ، وأبُو حَنِيفَةَ، وغَيْرُهم، وهو ظاهِرُ قَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَمَن قَتَلَهُ مِنكم مُتَعَمِّدًا﴾ الآيَةَ؛ لِأنَّ تَكْرارَ القَتْلِ يَقْتَضِي تَكْرارَ الجَزاءِ. وقالَ بَعْضُ العُلَماءِ: لا يُحْكَمُ عَلَيْهِ بِالجَزاءِ إلّا مَرَّةً واحِدَةً، فَإنْ عادَ لِقَتْلِهِ مَرَّةً ثانِيَةً لَمْ يُحْكَمْ عَلَيْهِ، وقِيلَ لَهُ: ﴿يَنْتَقِمُ اللَّهُ مِنكَ﴾؛ لِقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿وَمَن عادَ فَيَنْتَقِمُ اللَّهُ مِنهُ﴾.
وَيُرْوى هَذا القَوْلُ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، وبِهِ قالَ الحَسَنُ، وإبْراهِيمُ، ومُجاهِدٌ، وشُرَيْحٌ، كَما نَقَلَهُ عَنْهُمُ القُرْطُبِيُّ، ورُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ أيْضًا أنَّهُ يَضْرِبُ حَتّى يَمُوتَ.

* *

المَسْألَةُ السّابِعَةُ: إذا دَلَّ المُحْرِمُ حَلالًا عَلى صَيْدٍ فَقَتَلَهُ، فَهَلْ يَجِبُ عَلى المُحْرِمِ جَزاءٌ؛ لِتَسَبُّبِهِ في قَتْلِ الحَلالِ لِلصَّيْدِ بِدَلالَتِهِ لَهُ عَلَيْهِ أوْ لا؟ اخْتَلَفَ العُلَماءُ في ذَلِكَ، فَذَهَبَ الإمامُ أحْمَدُ، وأبُو حَنِيفَةَ إلى أنَّ المُحْرِمَ الدّالَّ يَلْزَمُهُ جَزاؤُهُ كامِلًا، ويُرْوى نَحْوُ ذَلِكَ عَنْ عَلِيٍّ، وابْنِ عَبّاسٍ، وعَطاءٍ، ومُجاهِدٍ، وبَكْرٍ المُزَنِيِّ، وإسْحاقَ. ويَدُلُّ لِهَذا القَوْلِ سُؤالُ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ أصْحابَهُ: ”«هَلْ أشارَ أحَدٌ مِنهم إلى أبِي قَتادَةَ عَلى الحِمارِ الوَحْشِيِّ»؟“.

فَإنَّ ظاهِرَهُ أنَّهم لَوْ دَلُّوهُ عَلَيْهِ كانَ بِمَثابَةِ ما لَوْ صادُوهُ في تَحْرِيمِ الأكْلِ؛ ويُفْهَمُ مِن (p-٤٤١)ذَلِكَ لُزُومُ الجَزاءِ، والقاعِدَةُ لُزُومُ الضَّمانِ لِلْمُتَسَبِّبِ إنْ لَمْ يُمْكِنْ تَضْمِينُ المُباشِرِ، والمُباشِرُ هُنا لا يُمْكِنُ تَضْمِينُهُ الصَّيْدَ؛ لِأنَّهُ حَلالٌ، والدّالُّ مُتَسَبِّبٌ. وهَذا القَوْلُ هو الأظْهَرُ. والَّذِينَ قالُوا بِهِ مِنهم مَن أطْلَقَ الدَّلالَةَ، ومِنهم مَنِ اشْتَرَطَ خَفاءَ الصَّيْدِ بِحَيْثُ لا يَراهُ دُونَ الدَّلالَةِ، كَأبِي حَنِيفَةَ. وقالَ الإمامُ الشّافِعِيُّ وأصْحابُهُ: لا شَيْءَ عَلى الدّالِ.

وَرُوِيَ عَنْ مالِكٍ نَحْوُهُ، قالُوا: لِأنَّ الصَّيْدَ يُضْمَنُ بِقَتْلِهِ، وهو لَمْ يَقْتُلْهُ. وإذا عَلِمَ المُحْرِمُ أنَّ الحَلالَ صادَهُ مِن أجْلِهِ فَأكَلَ مِنهُ؛ فَعَلَيْهِ الجَزاءُ كامِلًا عِنْدَ مالِكٍ، كَما صَرَّحَ بِذَلِكَ في ”المُوَطَّإِ“ (al-Muwatta', كتاب الإمام مالك في الحديث والفقه). وأمّا إذا دَلَّ المُحْرِمُ مُحْرِمًا آخَرَ عَلى الصَّيْدِ فَقَتَلَهُ، فَقالَ بَعْضُ العُلَماءِ: عَلَيْهِما جَزاءٌ واحِدٌ بَيْنَهُما، وهو مَذْهَبُ الإمامِ أحْمَدَ، وبِهِ قالَ عَطاءٌ، وحَمّادُ بْنُ أبِي سُلَيْمانَ، كَما نَقَلَهُ عَنْهُمُ ابْنُ قُدامَةَ في ”المُغْنِي“. وقالَ بَعْضُ العُلَماءِ: عَلى كُلِّ واحِدٍ مِنهُما جَزاءٌ كامِلٌ، وبِهِ قالَ الشَّعْبِيُّ، وسَعِيدُ بْنُ جُبَيْرٍ، والحارِثُ العُكْلِيُّ، وأصْحابُ الرَّأْيِ، كَما نَقَلَهُ عَنْهم أيْضًا صاحِبُ ”المُغْنِي“.

وَقالَ بَعْضُ العُلَماءِ: الجَزاءُ كُلُّهُ عَلى المُحْرِمِ المُباشِرِ، ولَيْسَ عَلى المُحْرِمِ الدّالِّ شَيْءٌ، وهَذا قَوْلُ الشّافِعِيِّ، ومالِكٍ، وهو الجارِي عَلى قاعِدَةِ تَقْدِيمِ المُباشِرِ عَلى المُتَسَبِّبِ في الضَّمانِ، والمُباشِرُ هُنا يُمْكِنُ تَضْمِينُهُ؛ لِأنَّهُ مُحْرِمٌ، وهَذا هو الأظْهَرُ. وعَلَيْهِ: فَعَلى الدّالِ الِاسْتِغْفارُ والتَّوْبَةُ. وبِهَذا تَعْرِفُ حُكْمَ ما لَوْ دَلَّ مُحْرِمٌ مُحْرِمًا، ثُمَّ دَلَّ هَذا الثّانِي مُحْرِمًا ثالِثًا، وهَكَذا، فَقَتَلَهُ الأخِيرُ؛ إذْ لا يَخْفى مِنَ الكَلامِ المُتَقَدِّمِ أنَّهم عَلى القَوْلِ الأوَّلِ شُرَكاءُ في جَزاءٍ واحِدٍ.
وَعَلى الثّانِي، عَلى كُلِّ واحِدٍ مِنهم جَزاءٌ، وعَلى الثّالِثِ، لا شَيْءَ إلّا عَلى مَن باشَرَ القَتْلَ.

* *

المَسْألَةُ الثّامِنَةُ: إذا اشْتَرَكَ مُحْرِمُونَ في قَتْلِ صَيْدٍ بِأنْ باشَرُوا قَتْلَهُ كُلَّهم، كَما إذا حَذَفُوهُ بِالحِجارَةِ والعِصِيِّ حَتّى ماتَ، فَقالَ مالِكٌ وأبُو حَنِيفَةَ: عَلى كُلِّ واحِدٍ مِنهم جَزاءٌ كامِلٌ، كَما لَوْ قَتَلَتْ جَماعَةٌ واحِدًا، فَإنَّهم يُقْتَلُونَ بِهِ جَمِيعًا؛ لِأنَّ كُلَّ واحِدٍ قاتِلٌ.
وَكَذَلِكَ هُنا كُلُّ واحِدٍ قاتِلٌ صَيْدًا فَعَلَيْهِ جَزاءٌ. وقالَ الشّافِعِيُّ ومَن وافَقَهُ: عَلَيْهِمْ كُلِّهِمْ جَزاءٌ واحِدٌ؛ لِقَضاءِ عُمَرَ، وعَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ، قالَهُ القُرْطُبِيُّ. ثُمَّ قالَ أيْضًا: ورَوى الدّارَقُطْنِيُّ: أنَّ مَوالِيَ لِابْنِ الزُّبَيْرِ أحْرَمُوا فَمَرَّتْ بِهِمْ ضُبُعٌ فَحَذَفُوها بِعِصِيِّهِمْ فَأصابُوها، (p-٤٤٢)فَوَقَعَ في أنْفُسِهِمْ، فَأتَوُا ابْنَ عُمَرَ، فَذَكَرُوا لَهُ ذَلِكَ، فَقالَ: عَلَيْكم كُلُّكم كَبْشٌ. قالُوا: أوَعَلى كُلِّ واحِدٍ مِنّا كَبْشٌ؟ قالَ: إنَّكم لَمُعَزَّزٌ بِكم عَلَيْكم كُلُّكم كَبْشٌ. قالَ اللُّغَوِيُّونَ: لَمُعَزَّزٌ بِكم أيْ لَمُشَدَّدٌ عَلَيْكم.
وَرُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ في قَوْمٍ أصابُوا ضَبُعًا فَقالَ: عَلَيْهِمْ كَبْشٌ يَتَخارَجُونَهُ بَيْنَهم. ودَلِيلُنا قَوْلُ اللَّهِ سُبْحانَهُ: ﴿وَمَن قَتَلَهُ مِنكم مُتَعَمِّدًا فَجَزاءٌ مِثْلُ ما قَتَلَ مِنَ النَّعَمِ﴾، وهَذا خِطابٌ لِكُلِّ قاتِلٍ. وكُلُّ واحِدٍ مِنَ القاتِلِينَ الصَّيْدَ قاتِلٌ نَفْسًا عَلى التَّمامِ والكَمالِ؛ بِدَلِيلِ قَتْلِ الجَماعَةِ بِالواحِدِ، ولَوْلا ذَلِكَ ما وجَبَ عَلَيْهِمُ القِصاصُ، وقَدْ قُلْنا بِوُجُوبِهِ إجْماعًا مِنّا ومِنهم، فَثَبَتَ ما قُلْناهُ.
وَقالَ أبُو حَنِيفَةَ: إذا قَتَلَ جَماعَةٌ صَيْدًا في الحَرَمِ وهم مُحِلُّونَ؛ فَعَلَيْهِمْ جَزاءٌ واحِدٌ، بِخِلافِ ما لَوْ قَتَلَهُ المُحْرِمُونَ في الحِلِّ أوِ الحَرَمِ؛ فَإنَّ ذَلِكَ لا يَخْتَلِفُ.
وَقالَ مالِكٌ: عَلى كُلِّ واحِدٍ مِنهم جَزاءٌ كامِلٌ؛ بِناءً عَلى أنَّ الرَّجُلَ يَكُونُ مُحْرِمًا بِدُخُولِهِ الحَرَمَ، كَما يَكُونُ مُحْرِمًا بِتَلْبِيَتِهِ بِالإحْرامِ، وكُلُّ واحِدٍ مِنَ الفِعْلَيْنِ قَدْ أكْسَبَهُ صِفَةً تَعَلَّقَ بِها نَهْيٌ، فَهو هاتِكٌ لَها في الحالَتَيْنِ.
وَحُجَّةُ أبِي حَنِيفَةَ ما ذَكَرَهُ القاضِي أبُو زَيْدٍ الدَّبُّوسِيُّ، قالَ: السِّرُّ فِيهِ أنَّ الجِنايَةَ في الإحْرامِ عَلى العِبادَةِ، وقَدِ ارْتَكَبَ كُلُّ واحِدٍ مِنهم مَحْظُورَ إحْرامِهِ.
وَإذا قَتَلَ المُحِلُّونَ صَيْدًا في الحَرَمِ، فَإنَّما أتْلَفُوا دابَّةً مُحْتَرَمَةً، بِمَنزِلَةِ ما لَوْ أتْلَفَ جَماعَةٌ دابَّةً؛ فَإنَّ كُلَّ واحِدٍ مِنهم قاتِلٌ دابَّةً، ويَشْتَرِكُونَ في القِيمَةِ. قالَ ابْنُ العَرَبِيِّ: وأبُو حَنِيفَةَ أقْوى مِنّا، وهَذا الدَّلِيلُ يَسْتَهِينُ بِهِ عُلَماؤُنا وهو عَسِيرُ الِانْفِصالِ عَلَيْنا. اهـ. مِنَ القُرْطُبِيِّ.

* *

المَسْألَةُ التّاسِعَةُ: اعْلَمْ أنَّ الصَّيْدَ يَنْقَسِمُ إلى قِسْمَيْنِ: قِسْمٌ لَهُ مِثْلٌ مِنَ النَّعَمِ كَبَقَرَةِ الوَحْشِ، وقِسْمٌ لا مِثْلَ لَهُ مِنَ النَّعَمِ كالعَصافِيرِ.

وَجُمْهُورُ العُلَماءِ يَعْتَبِرُونَ المِثْلِيَّةَ بِالمُماثَلَةِ في الصُّورَةِ والخِلْقَةِ، وخالَفَ الإمامُ أبُو حَنِيفَةَ - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ تَعالى - الجُمْهُورَ، فَقالَ: إنَّ المُماثَلَةَ مَعْنَوِيَّةٌ، وهي القِيمَةُ، أيْ قِيمَةُ الصَّيْدِ في المَكانِ الَّذِي قَتَلَهُ فِيهِ، أوْ أقْرَبِ مَوْضِعٍ إلَيْهِ إنْ كانَ لا يُباعُ الصَّيْدُ في مَوْضِعِ قَتْلِهِ، فَيَشْتَرِي بِتِلْكَ القِيمَةِ هَدْيًا إنْ شاءَ، أوْ يَشْتَرِي بِها طَعامًا، ويُطْعِمُ المَساكِينَ كُلَّ (p-٤٤٣)مِسْكِينٍ نِصْفَ صاعٍ مِن بُرٍّ، أوْ صاعًا مِن شَعِيرٍ، أوْ صاعًا مِن تَمْرٍ.

واحْتَجَّ أبُو حَنِيفَةَ - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ - بِأنَّهُ لَوْ كانَ الشَّبَهُ مِن طَرِيقِ الخِلْقَةِ والصُّورَةِ مُعْتَبَرًا لَكانَ في النَّعامَةِ بَدَنَةً، وفي الحِمارِ بَقَرَةً، وفي الظَّبْيِ شاةً؛ ولَما أوْقَفَهُ عَلى عَدْلَيْنِ يَحْكُمانِ بِهِ؛ لِأنَّ ذَلِكَ قَدْ عُلِمَ فَلا يُحْتاجُ إلى الِارْتِياءِ والنَّظَرِ، وإنَّما يَفْتَقِرُ إلى العَدْلَيْنِ والنَّظَرِ ما تَشَكَّلَ الحالُ فِيهِ، ويَخْتَلِفُ فِيهِ وجْهُ النَّظَرِ.

وَدَلِيلُ الجُمْهُورِ عَلى أنَّ المُرادَ بِالمِثْلِ مِنَ النَّعَمِ: المُشابَهَةُ لِلصَّيْدِ في الخِلْقَةِ والصُّورَةِ مِنها، قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿فَجَزاءٌ مِثْلُ ما قَتَلَ مِنَ النَّعَمِ﴾ الآيَةَ، فالمِثْلُ يَقْتَضِي بِظاهِرِهِ المِثْلَ الخِلْقِيَّ الصُّورِيَّ دُونَ المَعْنَوِيِّ، ثُمَّ قالَ: ﴿مِنَ النَّعَمِ﴾، فَصَرَّحَ بِبَيانِ جِنْسِ المِثْلِ، ثُمَّ قالَ: ﴿يَحْكُمُ بِهِ ذَوا عَدْلٍ مِنكُمْ﴾، وضَمِيرُ ﴿بِهِ﴾ راجِعٌ إلى المِثْلِ مِنَ النَّعَمِ؛ لِأنَّهُ لَمْ يَتَقَدَّمْ ذِكْرٌ لِسِواهُ حَتّى يَرْجِعَ إلَيْهِ الضَّمِيرُ.
ثُمَّ قالَ: ﴿هَدْيًا بالِغَ الكَعْبَةِ﴾، والَّذِي يُتَصَوَّرُ أنْ يَكُونَ هَدْيًا مِثْلَ المَقْتُولِ مِنَ النَّعَمِ، فَأمّا القِيمَةُ فَلا يُتَصَوَّرُ أنْ تَكُونَ هَدْيًا، ولا جَرى لَها ذِكْرٌ في نَفْسِ الآيَةِ، وادِّعاءُ أنَّ المُرادَ شِراءُ الهَدْيِ بِها يُعِيدُ مِن ظاهِرِ الآيَةِ، فاتَّضَحَ أنَّ المُرادَ مِثْلٌ مِنَ النَّعَمِ. وقَوْلُهُ: لَوْ كانَ الشَّبَهُ الخِلْقِيُّ مُعْتَبَرًا لَما أوْقَفَهُ عَلى عَدْلَيْنِ؟، أُجِيبَ عَنْهُ: بِأنَّ اعْتِبارَ العَدْلَيْنِ إنَّما وجَبَ لِلنَّظَرِ في حالِ الصَّيْدِ مِن كِبَرٍ وصِغَرٍ، وما لا جِنْسَ لَهُ مِمّا لَهُ جِنْسٌ، وإلْحاقُ ما لَمْ يَقَعْ عَلَيْهِ نَصٌّ بِما وقَعَ عَلَيْهِ النَّصُّ. قالَهُ القُرْطُبِيُّ.

قالَ مُقَيِّدُهُ - عَفا اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: المُرادُ بِالمِثْلِيَّةِ في الآيَةِ التَّقْرِيبُ، وإذًا فَنَوْعُ المُماثَلَةِ قَدْ يَكُونُ خَفِيًّا، لا يَطَّلِعُ عَلَيْهِ إلّا أهْلُ المَعْرِفَةِ والفِطْنَةِ التّامَّةِ، كَكَوْنِ الشّاةِ مَثَلًا لِلْحَمامَةِ؛ لِمُشابَهَتِها لَها في عَبِّ الماءِ والهَدِيرِ.

And when you have understood the verification (taḥqīq) regarding the requital in kind (jazā' bi-l-mithl) from livestock, know that the one who kills game (qātil al-ṣayd) has a choice between it, the feeding of the poor (iṭ'ām), and fasting (ṣiyām), as is the plain meaning of the noble verse, because "aw" (or) is a particle of choice (ḥarf takhyīr). Allah, exalted is He, has said: ﴿or an expiation: feeding needy people, or the equivalent of that in fasting﴾. This is also the view of the majority of scholars (jumhūr al-'ulamā').

If he chooses the requital in kind from livestock, it is obligatory to slaughter it within the Sacred Precinct (al-Ḥaram) specifically, because it is a right of the needy of the Ḥaram, and it is not valid elsewhere, as Allah, exalted is He, stipulated with His words: ﴿as an offering (hady) reaching the Ka'bah﴾. The intended meaning is the whole Ḥaram, as in His words: ﴿Then its place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 33], although the principal place of sacrifice (al-manḥar al-akbar) is Minā.

If he chooses the feeding, Mālik said: "The best I have heard concerning it is that the game is valued in food, and he feeds each needy person one mudd (a measure of grain), or fasts one day in place of each mudd." (p-444)

Ibn al-Qāsim reported from him: "If he values the game in dirhams, then values the dirhams in food, it suffices him." The correct view is the first. If less than a mudd remains, he gives it in charity according to some scholars, and completes it to a full mudd according to others. As for if he fasts, he completes the broken day without any disagreement.

Al-Shāfi'ī said: "If he chooses feeding or fasting, the game that has a counterpart (mithl) is not valued. Rather, its counterpart from livestock is valued in dirhams, then the dirhams are valued in food, and he feeds each needy person one mudd, or fasts one day for each mudd, and completes the broken portion."

The verification is that the choice belongs to the killer of the game, who is the one paying the requital.

Some scholars said: the choice belongs to the two just judges (al-'adlān al-ḥakamān). Others said: it is proper for the two arbitrators, if they judge by the counterpart, to give the killer of the game the choice among the three mentioned.

Some scholars said: if they judge by the counterpart, it is binding on him. The Qur'an is explicit that the counterpart from livestock is not binding on him unless he chooses it over feeding and fasting, due to the choice stipulated by the particle of choice in the verse.

Some scholars said: the options are in sequence (al-tartīb): the obligation is the hady; if he does not find it, then feeding; if he does not find that, then fasting. This is reported from Ibn 'Abbās, al-Nakha'ī and others. It is not hidden that this contradicts the apparent meaning of the Qur'an without evidence.

Abū Ḥanīfah said: he fasts one day for every two mudd, by analogy with the expiation for harm (fidyat al-adhā), as reported by al-Qurṭubī. Know that the apparent meaning of this noble verse is that he fasts the equivalent of the stated food, even if the fasting exceeds two or three months.

Some scholars said: the fasting of the requital does not exceed two months, because they are the highest of the expiations (kaffārāt). Ibn al-'Arabī chose this, and it has a basis in reasoning, but the apparent meaning of the verse contradicts it.

Yaḥyā ibn 'Umar of the Mālikīs said: "It is only said: how many men does this game satisfy? He knows the number, then it is said: how much food equals this number? If he wishes, he gives that food; if he wishes, he fasts the number of its mudds." Al-Qurṭubī said: "This is a good view, one that is cautious, because the value of the game in food may be small, so by this consideration the feeding increases."

(p-445) Know that of the three types, one requires the Ḥaram by consensus, which is the hady as previously explained. One does not require the Ḥaram by consensus, which is fasting. And one is disputed, which is feeding. Some scholars held that one feeds only within the Ḥaram; some held that he feeds in the place where the game was hit; and some held that he feeds wherever he wishes. The most evident of these is that it is a right of the needy of the Ḥaram, because it is a substitute for the hady or its equivalent, and it is a right of theirs by consensus, as Allah, exalted is He, stated with His words: ﴿as an offering reaching the Ka'bah﴾. As for fasting, it is an act of worship specific to the one fasting, in which no created being has a right, so he may perform it in any place he wishes.

If the game has no counterpart from livestock, such as sparrows, then it is valued, and its value is then known in food, and he gives for each needy person one mudd, or fasts one day for each mudd.

Thus it is established that what has a counterpart from livestock is subject to a choice among three things: the hady with its counterpart, feeding, and fasting. And what has no counterpart is subject to a choice between two things only: feeding and fasting, as we have mentioned.

Know that the counterpart from livestock has three states:

The first: that a ruling has preceded concerning it from the Prophet (ﷺ).

The second: that a ruling has preceded concerning it from two just men among the Companions (al-Ṣaḥābah) or the Successors (al-Tābi'ūn), for example.

The third: that no ruling has preceded concerning it either from him (ﷺ) or from them (may Allah be pleased with them). As for that concerning which the Prophet (ﷺ) ruled, it is not permitted for anyone to rule concerning it otherwise. This is like the hyena (al-ḍaba'), for the Prophet (ﷺ) judged concerning it with a ram (kabsh). Ibn Ḥajar said in "al-Talkhīṣ," the following text: The hadith that "the Prophet (ﷺ) judged concerning the hyena with a ram" was recorded by the authors of the Sunan, Ibn Ḥibbān, Aḥmad, and al-Ḥākim in "al-Mustadrak," through the route of 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī 'Ammār, from Jābir, with the wording: "I asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the hyena, and he said: 'It is game, and a ram is prescribed for it if the one in ihram hits it.'" The wording of al-Ḥākim is: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prescribed for the hyena that the one in ihram hits a ram," and its being game. It is also in Ibn Mājah, except that he did not say "najdī." al-Tirmidhī said: "I asked al-Bukhārī about it and he authenticated it." Likewise 'Abd al-Ḥaqq authenticated it, though it has been faulted for being mawqūf (stopping at a Companion). al-Bayhaqī said: "It is a good hadith on which the proof rests." Al-Bayhaqī narrated it through the route of al-Ajlaḥ, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Jābir, from 'Umar, who said: "I do not think he raised it except that he (ﷺ) ruled concerning the hyena with a ram..." the hadith. al-Shāfi'ī narrated it from Mālik, from Abū al-Zubayr, with the same, as a mawqūf report, and al-Dāraquṭnī authenticated its being mawqūf in this chapter. (p-446) al-Dāraquṭnī and al-Ḥākim narrated it through the route of Ibrāhīm al-Ṣā'igh, from 'Aṭā', from Jābir who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The hyena is game; if the one in ihram hits it, there is an aged ram in it, and it is eaten." On this subject, from Ibn 'Abbās, al-Dāraquṭnī and al-Bayhaqī narrated it through the route of 'Amr ibn Abī 'Amr, from 'Ikrimah, from him, and it has been faulted for being mursal (with a missing Companion in the chain).

al-Shāfi'ī narrated it through the route of Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ikrimah, as mursal, and said: "Such a report would not be established if it stood alone." Then he reinforced it with the hadith of Ibn Abī 'Ammār mentioned earlier. al-Bayhaqī said: "It is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbās as mawqūf."

The author of this commentary, may Allah pardon him, says: The Prophet's (ﷺ) judgment with a ram is established, as you have seen, by the authentication of al-Bukhārī and 'Abd al-Ḥaqq of it, and likewise al-Bayhaqī, al-Shāfi'ī, and others. A hadith that is authenticated in one chain is not harmed by the mursal or mawqūf report in another route, as is the correct view among the scholars of hadith, because the connecting (waṣl) and raising (rafʿ) are additions, and the addition of a trustworthy narrator is accepted, as is well known. It is to this that the author of "Marāqī al-Su'ūd" refers in his words:

"The raising, the connecting, and the addition of wording are accepted by the imam of memorization..."
... etc. ...

As for if a ruling has preceded concerning it from two just men among the Companions or those after them, some scholars said: one follows their ruling, and there is no need for two just men to consider it and rule anew, because Allah said: ﴿judged by two just men among you﴾ [al-Mā'idah: 95], and they have ruled that this is the counterpart of that.

Some scholars said: a new ruling by two just men is necessary, and among those who said this is Mālik. al-Qurṭubī said: "Even if he were content with the ruling of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them), it would be good."

It is also reported from Mālik that he requires a new ruling for every game except the pigeons of Makkah, the wild donkey, the gazelle, and the ostrich; for these he suffices with the ruling of those who came before from the predecessors (al-salaf). It is reported from 'Umar that he and 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn 'Awf ruled concerning a gazelle with a she-goat ('anz), narrated by Mālik, al-Bayhaqī, and others. It is reported from 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn 'Awf and Sa'd (may Allah be pleased with them both) that they ruled concerning the gazelle with a male goat (tays a'far). And from Ibn 'Abbās, 'Umar, 'Uthmān, 'Alī, Zayd ibn Thābit, Mu'āwiyah, Ibn Mas'ūd, and others, that they said: "For the ostrich, a camel (badanah)," narrated by al-Bayhaqī and others. And from Ibn 'Abbās and others: that for the wild donkey and the cow, a cow; and that for the deer (al-ayyil), a cow.

(p-447) From Jābir: that 'Umar judged concerning the hyena with a ram, for the gazelle with a she-goat, for the hare with a female kid (anāq), and for the jerboa with a yearling (jafrah), narrated by Mālik, al-Bayhaqī. al-Ajlaḥ ibn 'Abd Allāh narrated this report from Jābir, from the Prophet (ﷺ), but the correct version is mawqūf upon 'Umar, as al-Bayhaqī and others mentioned. al-Bayhaqī said: "Likewise 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abī Sulaymān narrated it from 'Aṭā', from Jābir, from 'Umar, as his own statement." From Ibn 'Abbās: that he judged concerning the hare with a female kid, and said: "It walks on four, and the female kid does likewise; it eats trees, and the female kid does likewise; it chews the cud, and the female kid does likewise," narrated by al-Bayhaqī.

From Ibn Mas'ūd: that he judged concerning the jerboa with a ḥafr or a jafrah, also narrated by al-Bayhaqī. al-Bayhaqī said: Abū 'Ubayd said: Abū Zayd said: the jafr is the young of goats which has reached four months and has been weaned from its mother. From Shurayḥ that he said: "If I had an arbitrator with me, I would judge concerning the fox with a young male goat (jadī)." It is reported from 'Aṭā' that he said: "For the fox there is a sheep (shāh)." It is reported from 'Umar and Arbad (may Allah be pleased with them both) that they judged concerning a lizard (ḍabb) killed by the aforementioned Arbad with a young male goat that had gathered water and trees, narrated by al-Bayhaqī and others.

From 'Uthmān ibn 'Affān (may Allah be pleased with him): that he judged concerning the umm ḥubayn with jillān from the sheep, and the jillān is the young male goat. Narrated by al-Bayhaqī and others.

Note:
The least that can be a requital from livestock according to Mālik is a sheep that is valid as a sacrificial animal (ḍaḥiyyah). So for him there is no requital with a jafrah or an 'anāq. He argues that the requital for game is like blood-money (diyah), in which there is no distinction between the young and the old, and that Allah said: ﴿an offering reaching the Ka'bah﴾, so the requital must be something valid as a hady. Thus for the lizard and the jerboa, its value in food is due according to him.

The author of this commentary, may Allah pardon him, says: The view of the majority concerning the requital of the young with the young and the old with the old is the apparent one, and it is the apparent meaning of His words: ﴿then the requital is the like of what he killed of livestock﴾. Ibn al-'Arabī said: "This is correct, and it is the choice of our scholars," meaning the view of the majority, which is the consideration of youth, age, illness, and the like, as with all other destroyed property.

* *

The tenth issue: if what the one in ihram destroyed is eggs. Mālik said: for the eggs of the ostrich, one-tenth of the price of a camel (badanah), and for the eggs of the Meccan pigeon, one-tenth of the price of a sheep. Ibn al-Qāsim said: it is the same whether there is a chick in them or not, as long as the chick has not cried out after breaking out. If it cries out, then the full requital is due, like the requital for the adult of that bird. Ibn al-Mawwāz said: by the judgment of two just men. Most scholars hold that for the egg of every bird its value is due.

(p-448)

The author of this commentary, may Allah pardon him, says: This is the more apparent view. al-Qurṭubī said: 'Ikrimah narrated from Ibn 'Abbās, from Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah: "That the Prophet (ﷺ) judged concerning an ostrich egg that was hit by one in ihram with its value," narrated by al-Dāraquṭnī. Abū Hurayrah narrated: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "For an ostrich egg, a day's fast or the feeding of one needy person," as al-Qurṭubī said.

If the one in ihram kills an elephant, it is said: for it is a camel of the large Hijān camels that have two humps. If none of these camels is found, then its value in food is considered, and that is due from him.

Al-Qurṭubī said: The practice concerning it is to place the elephant in a boat and observe the point to which the boat sinks in the water, then the elephant is removed, and food is placed in the boat up to the limit to which it sank with the elephant in it. This is its equivalent in food. As for if one considers its value, it has a great price because of its bones and tusks, so the food would be much, and that is harmful. End quote.

The author of this commentary, may Allah pardon him, says: What al-Qurṭubī mentioned concerning considering the like of the elephant as food involves two matters:

The first: it is generally not within the capacity of people to do this, since transporting the elephant to the water, obtaining a boat, lifting the elephant into it, and removing it from it are beyond the ability of ordinary people in most cases. General obligation should only be imposed with what is generally within the capacity of everyone.

The second: the great value of the animal is not considered a hardship, because he is only required to pay the value of what he destroyed while in the state of ihram. Whoever destroys a large animal while in ihram is obligated to pay a large compensation, and this is not a hardship for him, because the greatness of the compensation follows the greatness of the offence, as is clear.

* *

**The eleventh issue:** The scholars agreed (ijma', scholarly consensus) that hunting in the Sacred Precinct of Makkah (haram, the sanctuary) is forbidden, and that cutting its trees and plants is unlawful, except for izkhir (a fragrant grass, idhkhir). This is based on the words of the Prophet (ﷺ) on the day of the conquest of Makkah: "This city is sacred. Its thorny plants may not be cut, its grass may not be pulled up, its game may not be frightened, and its lost property may not be picked up except by one who announces it." Al-Abbas said: "Except the izkhir, for they need it, for it is used for their graves and houses." So he said: "Except the izkhir." (Agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim, from the hadith of Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father.) And from Abu Hurayrah: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) conquered Makkah, he said: 'Its game may not be frightened, its thorny plants may not be pulled up, and its fallen items may not be taken except by one who announces them.' Al-Abbas said: 'Except the izkhir, for we use it for our graves and houses.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Except the izkhir.'" (Also agreed upon.) In one wording, "its trees may not be cut" replaces "its thorny plants may not be pulled up." The hadiths on this subject are numerous.

Know that the trees and plants of the Haram fall into three categories: one extreme and an intermediate category where cutting is not permitted by consensus, which is what Allah caused to grow in the Haram without human agency; and an extreme where cutting is permitted by consensus, which is what humans planted, such as crops, vegetables, herbs and the like; and a category on which scholars differ, which is what humans planted of non-edible and non-fragrant kinds, such as the athl (tamarisk) and the 'awsaj (a thorny shrub). Most scholars permit cutting it.

Some scholars, including al-Shafi'i, prohibited it, as this is more cautious for fulfilling the obligation. Some scholars said: if it first grew outside the Haram, then was uprooted and planted within the Haram, its cutting is permitted; but if it first grew within the Haram, its cutting is not permitted. The thorny plants and the 'awsaj are unlawful to cut, according to Ibn Qudamah in al-Mughni. Al-Qadi and Abu al-Khattab said: it is not unlawful. This was narrated from 'Ata', Mujahid, 'Amr ibn Dinar and al-Shafi'i, because it harms by its nature, and so it resembles predatory animals.

The compiler of this work, may Allah forgive him, says: The analogy of the thorny plants of the Haram to predatory beasts is rejected on two grounds:

The first: predatory beasts attack and target people, unlike thorny plants.

The second: it contradicts the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "Its thorny plants may not be cut." An analogy that contradicts a explicit text is invalid in its reasoning. In Maraqi al-Su'ud (verse in rajaz meter):
"Disagreement against an explicit text or a consensus
produces invalid reasoning, as every learned person knows."
Invalid reasoning is a flaw that nullifies the evidence, as established in the principles of jurisprudence.

Scholars differed about cutting dry trees and grass. Some scholars permitted it, and this is the position of al-Shafi'i and Ahmad, because it is like dead game: there is no penalty on one who splits it in two. This is the apparent meaning of the Prophet's (ﷺ) words: "Its khala (fresh grass) may not be pulled up," since khala is the moist plant, so it is understood that there is no harm in cutting the dry.

Some scholars said: it is not permitted to cut its dry parts. They argued that the exception of izkhir indicates the prohibition of dry plants, and that in some transmissions of the hadith of Abu Hurayrah: "Its hashish may not be gathered," and in the language hashish means dry herbage. There is no doubt that leaving it is more cautious.

Scholars also differed on whether it is permitted to let animals graze there. Abu Hanifah prohibited it, and something similar was narrated from Malik. From Ahmad there are two reports. The position of al-Shafi'i is that it is permitted. Those who prohibited it argued that whatever is forbidden to destroy may not be given over to something that destroys it, like game. Those who permitted it argued with two points:

The first: the hadith of Ibn Abbas, who said: "I came riding a donkey and found the Prophet (ﷺ) leading the people in prayer at Mina, without a wall, so I entered the row and let the donkey graze." (Agreed upon.) Mina is part of the Haram.

The second: sacrificial animals (hady) entered in large numbers during the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions, and no one is reported to have ordered that their mouths be stopped from eating the plants of the Haram. This view is more apparent, and Allah knows best.

'Ata' said this as well. Scholars differed on taking leaves and tooth-sticks (siwak) from the trees of the Haram, when taking the leaves does not harm the tree. Some scholars prohibited it, because of the general evidence. al-Shafi'i permitted it, because there is no harm to the tree. It was narrated from 'Ata' and 'Amr ibn Dinar that they permitted the leaves of senna for purgative use without uprooting it. The safest course is to avoid all of this. The apparent reasoning of those who permitted it is by analogy to izkhir, on the basis of the common need.

Ibn Qudamah said in al-Mughni: There is no harm in benefiting from branches that broke off and plants uprooted without human action, nor from fallen leaves. Ahmad stated this, and we know of no disagreement on it, because the report was only about cutting, and this was not cut. But if a human cut it, Ahmad said: "I have not heard that one may benefit from it if it was cut." He said regarding a large tree that is cut, by its resemblance to game, that one may not benefit from its wood. That is because it is forbidden to destroy it due to the sanctity of the Haram. If someone who is forbidden to cut it cuts it, he may not benefit from it, like game that a muhrim (one in ihram) slaughters.

It is possible that it is permitted for one who did not cut it to benefit from it, because it was cut without his action, so he is permitted to benefit from it, as if an animal had cut it. It differs from the game that he slaughtered, because slaughter requires the qualification of the one who slaughters, and this is why it is not valid when done by an animal, unlike this case. End of quote.

Ibn Qudamah also said in al-Mughni: It is permitted to pick truffles (kam'ah) from the Haram, and likewise the puffball (fiq'), because it has no root, so it resembles fruit. Harb related: "From the trees of the Haram one may eat the young cucumbers (dabaghis), the 'ishriq (a plant), and what fell from the trees, and what people planted."

Scholars differed about the grass of the Makkan Haram: is it permitted to take it for animal fodder? The more correct view is that it is prohibited, because of the general evidence.

Now that you understand this: if a non-muhrim kills game in the Makkan Haram, the majority of scholars, including the four imams and most jurists of the cities, hold that he must pay compensation (jaza'), like the compensation of the muhrim mentioned earlier. However, Abu Hanifah said: there is no fasting in it, because it is pure destruction without any forbidden act.

Dawud ibn 'Ali al-Zahiri disagreed with this, arguing that the default position is the absence of obligation (bara'at al-dhimmah), and no text is reported regarding compensation for game of the Haram, so it remains on the default principle that the obligation is absent. His view is very strong.

The majority argued that the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, ruled regarding pigeons of the Makkan Haram that a sheep must be given for each one. This was narrated from 'Umar, 'Uthman, 'Ali, Ibn 'Umar and Ibn Abbas, and no disagreement from anyone else is reported; so it is a silent consensus (ijma' sukuti). They also argued by analogy to the game of the muhrim, on the basis that all of it is game forbidden for the sake of Allah's right. What we have mentioned from the majority of scholars, that whatever a muhrim is liable for, one in the Haram is also liable for, has two exceptions:

The first: lice, for killing them is disputed during ihram, but it is permitted in the Haram without disagreement.

The second: aquatic game is permitted during ihram without disagreement. There is disagreement about hunting it from the wells and springs of the Haram. Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah disliked it, because of the general wording of the Prophet's (peace be upon him) saying: "Its game may not be frightened," so the sanctity of game is established by the sanctity of the place, and the apparent wording of the text includes every kind of game. It is also because it is game that does not harm, so it resembles gazelles. Some scholars permitted it, arguing that ihram does not prohibit it, so the Haram does not either. There are two reports from Imam Ahmad on this, one prohibiting and one permitting.

Likewise, scholars differed about the trees of the Makkan Haram and its fresh grass: is there a liability on one who cuts them? (p. 452)

A group of scholars, including Malik, Abu Thawr and Dawud, said: there is no liability for its trees and plants. Ibn al-Mundhir said: "I find no evidence obliging a fixed obligation regarding the trees of the Haram, from the Book, the Sunnah or consensus, and I say what Malik said: we seek Allah's forgiveness."

Those who held that there is liability include al-Shafi'i, Ahmad and Abu Hanifah, except that Abu Hanifah said: he must pay the full value. al-Shafi'i and Ahmad said: for a large tree he must pay a cow, for a small tree a sheep, for the fresh grass its value, and for a branch the amount by which the tree was diminished. If the cut part grows back, some said the liability falls away, and others said it does not.

Those who said that for a large tree (dawhah) there is a cow, and for a small tree (jazlah) a sheep, relied on reports narrated from some Companions, such as 'Umar and Ibn Abbas. The dawhah is the large tree, and the jazlah is the small one.

* *

**The twelfth issue:** The Sacred Precinct of Madinah. Know that the majority of scholars hold that Madinah is also a sanctuary, its game may not be frightened and its fresh grass may not be pulled up. Abu Hanifah disagreed with the majority, saying: the sanctuary of Madinah is not a sanctuary in the true sense, and the rulings of the sanctuary, such as the prohibition on killing game and cutting trees, do not apply to it. The clear and sound hadiths reject this view and establish that the area between the two lava plains (labatayn) of Madinah is a sanctuary, its game may not be frightened, and its fresh grass may not be pulled up except for fodder. Among these is the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Zayd ibn 'Asim, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ibrahim made Makkah sacred, and I have made Madinah sacred as Ibrahim made Makkah sacred." (The hadith is agreed upon.)

From Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made sacred what lies between the two lava plains of Madinah, and made twelve miles around Madinah a protected zone (himan)." (Also agreed upon.) Abu Hurayrah used to say: "If I saw gazelles grazing in Madinah, I would not frighten them."

Also from Abu Hurayrah regarding Madinah, he said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbid stripping its trees or cutting them." (Narrated by Imam Ahmad.)

From Anas: "The Prophet (ﷺ) overlooked Madinah and said: 'O Allah, I make sacred what lies between its two mountains, like what Ibrahim made sacred for Makkah. O Allah, bless them in their mudd and their sa'." (Agreed upon.)

Al-Bukhari related from him that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Madinah is sacred from such-and-such to such-and-such. Its trees may not be cut, and no innovation may be introduced in it. Whoever introduces an innovation in it, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels and all people." Muslim related from 'Asim al-Ahwal, who said: "I asked Anas: Did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) make Madinah sacred? He said: Yes, it is sacred; its fresh grass may not be pulled up." (The hadith is lengthy.)

From Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have made Madinah sacred. What lies between its two narrow passes (ma'zimayha) is sacred: no blood may be shed in it, no weapons may be carried in it, and no tree may be stripped in it except for fodder." (Narrated by Muslim.)

From Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Ibrahim made Makkah sacred, and I have made Madinah sacred between its two lava plains. Its thorny trees may not be cut and its game may not be hunted." (Also narrated by Muslim.)

From 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Madinah is sacred between 'Ayr and Thawr." (The hadith is agreed upon.)

From 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding Madinah: "Its fresh grass may not be pulled up, its game may not be frightened, and its lost property may not be picked up except by one who announces it. It is not lawful for a man to carry weapons in it for fighting, and it is not valid to cut a tree in it, except that a man may feed his camel." (Narrated by Abu Dawud with a sound chain, and also by Imam Ahmad.)

And from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I declare forbidden (ḥarrim) what lies between the two lava plains (al-Madina) of Madinah, that its thorny trees be cut or its game be hunted."

And he said: "Madinah is better for them, if only they knew. No one leaves it out of desire for something else except that Allah replaces him in it with someone better than him. And no one perseveres through its hardship and difficulty except that I will be a witness for him or an intercessor for him on the Day of Resurrection." Related by Muslim.

And from Rafi' ibn Khadij (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Ibrahim declared Makkah forbidden, and I declare forbidden what lies between its two lava plains." Also related by Muslim.

And from Sahl ibn Hunayf (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) pointed with his hand towards Madinah and said: 'Indeed it is a sanctuary (ḥaram) that is safe.'" Related by Muslim in his Sahih as well.

And from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Saʿid al-Khudri, from his father Abu Saʿid al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with them both): that he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "I have declared forbidden what lies between the two lava plains of Madinah, just as Ibrahim declared Makkah forbidden."

He said: Abu Saʿid al-Khudri used to find a bird in the hand of one of us, and he would take it and release it from his hand, then (p. 454) let it go. Related by Muslim in his Sahih as well.

And from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUbada al-Zuraqi: that he used to hunt sparrows in the well of Ihab, which belonged to them. He said: ʿUbada saw me when I had caught a sparrow, so he snatched it from me and released it, and said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "He declared forbidden what lies between its two lava plains just as Ibrahim (peace be upon him) declared Makkah forbidden." ʿUbada was one of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Related by al-Bayhaqi.

And from Ibrahim ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "I hunted a bird with a qunbula (a trap), and I went out with it in my hand. My father ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf met me and said: 'What is this in your hand?' I said: 'A bird I hunted with a qunbula.' So he pinched my ear hard, snatched it from my hand, released it, and said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) declared forbidden the game of what lies between its two lava plains.'" Related by al-Bayhaqi as well. The qunbula is an instrument used to hunt the nuhas, which is a bird.

And from Abu Ayyub al-Ansari (may Allah be pleased with him): that he found some boys who had cornered a fox in a corner, so he drove them away from it. Malik said: I do not know except that he said: "Is this done in the sanctuary of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" Related by al-Bayhaqi as well.

And from Zayd ibn Thabit (may Allah be pleased with him): "that he found a man at al-Aswaq, which is a place in Madinah, who had hunted a nuhas. Zayd took it from his hand and released it, then said: Do you not know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) declared forbidden the game of what lies between its two lava plains?" Related by al-Bayhaqi. The man who hunted the nuhas was Shurahbil ibn Saʿd. The nuhas, with a dammah on the nun and a fatha on the ha after it, followed by a silent sin, is a small bird larger than the sparrow, resembling the qunbara (lark).

The hadiths on this subject are very numerous. There is no doubt that the sound and explicit texts we have cited concerning the sanctuary of Madinah are beyond dispute, and there is no ambiguity that it is forbidden (ḥarām): its game must not be frightened, its trees must not be cut, and its grass must not be pulled up except for fodder. As for what some scholars argued as proof that it is not forbidden, from his (ﷺ) saying: "What did the little bird (nughayr) do, O Abu ʿUmayr?", there is no evidence in it, because it is open to the possibility that this was before Madinah was declared forbidden, and open to the possibility that the bird was hunted outside the sacred territory and then brought into Madinah.

Some scholars have used it as evidence for the permissibility of keeping game that was hunted outside the sacred territory and bringing it into Madinah. But what admits of these possibilities cannot override the sound, explicit, numerous texts that are free of ambiguity and possibility. Knowing this, be aware that the scholars who hold that Madinah is forbidden, and they are the majority of the scholars of the Ummah, disagreed concerning the game of the sanctuary of Madinah: does the one who kills it owe compensation (ḍamān) or not?
