(p. 455) The same applies to its trees. Many scholars, among them Malik, al-Shafiʿi in his later view (al-jadid), and their followers, and it is one of the two narrations from Ahmad, and most scholars hold it, say that it is a place that may be entered without ihram, so no penalty (jaza') is due for it, like the valley of Wajj.

They also used as evidence his (ﷺ) saying: "Madinah is a sanctuary between ʿAyr and Thawr. Whoever commits an offence (ḥadath) in it, or gives shelter to an offender in it, upon him is the curse of Allah, the angels and all people. Allah will not accept from him on the Day of Resurrection any voluntary act (ṣarf) or obligatory act (ʿadl)." So his mention of this severe threat in the Hereafter, without mentioning an expiation (kaffara) in this world, is evidence that no expiation is obligatory for it in this world, and this is clear.

Ibn Abi Dhi'b and Ibn al-Mundhir said: the penalty obligatory for game in the sanctuary of Madinah is the same as the penalty obligatory for game in the sanctuary of Makkah. This is also the older view of al-Shafiʿi. Those who hold this view argued that he (ﷺ) explicitly stated in the sound hadiths mentioned earlier that he declared Madinah forbidden like the declaration of Ibrahim for Makkah, and equivalence in the declaration of forbiddenness requires equality in the penalty for whoever violates the sanctity in either of them.

Al-Qurtubi said, quoting al-Qadi ʿAbd al-Wahhab: "This view is more analogous to our principles in my opinion, especially since Madinah is, according to our companions, superior to Makkah, and prayer in it is superior to prayer in the Sacred Mosque." End of quotation.

The author of this commentary (may Allah pardon him) says: The position of the majority on the superiority of Makkah, and that the multiplication of prayer in it is greater than in Madinah by a hundred-fold, is more apparent, since the evidence for it stands.

Some of those who held that a penalty is obligatory in the sanctuary of Madinah held that the penalty in it is the seizure of the spoils (salab) of the one who kills the game or cuts the trees in it.

The author of this commentary (may Allah pardon him) says: This view is the strongest in evidence, because of what Muslim related in his Sahih from Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas (may Allah be pleased with him): "that he rode to his estate at al-ʿAqiq, and found a slave cutting or stripping trees. So he took his spoils (salaba). When Saʿd returned, the slave's people came to him and asked him to return to their boy, or to them, what he had taken from their boy. He said: 'I seek refuge in Allah from returning something the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave me as a reward (nafalani).' And he refused to return it to them." Related by Muslim in his Sahih, and by Ahmad.

As for what al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir, may Allah have mercy on him, that this ruling is specific to Saʿd (may Allah be pleased with him), supporting this with the claim that his saying "nafalani" meaning "gave me," is apparent in being specific to him and not to others, there are two matters in my view:

(p. 456) The first: this is not sufficient to establish specificity, because the default is that people are equal in the legal rulings unless there is evidence. His saying "nafalani" is not evidence, because it is possible that he rewarded everyone who found a cutter of trees or a killer of game in Madinah with his clothing, just as he rewarded Saʿd, and this is the apparent meaning.

The second: Saʿd himself is narrated to have generalized the ruling and extended it to others. Imam Ahmad and Abu Dawud related from Sulayman ibn Abi ʿAbd Allah who said: "I saw Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas seize a man hunting in the sanctuary of Madinah which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) declared forbidden, and he took his clothing. His clients came to him, and he said: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) declared this sanctuary forbidden, and said: "Whoever you see hunting in it anything, then its spoils are yours." I will not return to you a provision the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave me as food. But if you wish, I will give you its price.'" In another wording: "Whoever seizes someone hunting in it, let him take his clothing." Al-Hakim also related this hadith and declared it sound, and it is explicit in generality and not specificity to Saʿd, as you see. In it is the explanation of the intended meaning of his saying "nafalani," and that it is general to everyone who finds someone doing that in it.

As for some people's weakening of this hadith on the ground that its chain includes Sulayman ibn Abi ʿAbd Allah, who is not acceptable, this is not valid, because Sulayman ibn Abi ʿAbd Allah is acceptable. Al-Dhahabi said of him: "A trustworthy Successor (tabi'i)." Ibn Hajar said of him in al-Taqrib: "acceptable (maqbul)."

The "acceptable" one, according to his definition in the introduction to his Taqrib, is one who has few narrations, and nothing is established against him that would require abandoning his hadith. So he is acceptable where he is followed (in narration), and otherwise he is "weak in hadith." Ibn Abi Hatim said of him: "He is not well known, but his hadith is considered (yuʿtabar)." End of quotation.

Sulayman ibn Abi ʿAbd Allah was followed in this hadith by ʿAmir ibn Saʿd in Muslim and Ahmad, and by a client of Saʿd in Abu Dawud. All of them narrate from Saʿd (may Allah be pleased with him). Thus the rejection of its weakening is clear, together with what we have mentioned: that al-Hakim declared it sound, and that al-Dhahabi said of him: "a trustworthy Successor."

What is meant by the spoils of the one who cuts trees or kills game in Madinah is taking his clothing. Some scholars said: even his trousers.

The apparent view is what some people of knowledge mentioned, that it is obligatory to leave what covers the severe nakedness ('awra mughallaza), and Allah knows best.

Some scholars said: the spoils here are the spoils of the killer. Concerning the disposal of these spoils there are three views:

(p. 457) The soundest is that they belong to the one who seized them, like the slain (in battle); its evidence is the hadith of Saʿd mentioned above.

The second: that they belong to the poor of Madinah.

The third: that they belong to the public treasury (bayt al-mal). The first view is the correct one.

The majority of scholars agree that the protected pasture (ḥima) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), mentioned in the hadith of Abu Hurayra agreed upon (by al-Bukhari and Muslim), whose extent is twelve miles in all directions from Madinah, is forbidden to cut its trees or pull up its grass, as related by Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The protected pasture of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is not to be beaten (for leaves) nor cut, but it may be lightly shaken gently." Related by Abu Dawud and al-Bayhaqi. Abu Dawud did not weaken it. What is known of Abu Dawud, may Allah have mercy on him, is that if he remains silent about a hadith, its lowest grade in his view is good (hasan).

Al-Nawawi said in Sharh al-Muhadhdhab after citing the hadith of Jabir: "Abu Dawud related it with a chain that is not strong, but he did not weaken it." End of quotation. This hadith is strengthened by what al-Bayhaqi related with his chain from Muhammad ibn Ziyad who said: "My grandfather was a client of ʿUthman ibn Maz'un, and he tended land belonging to ʿUthman in which there were herbs and cucumbers. He said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) would often come to me at midday, placing his garment on his head, inspecting the protected pasture to ensure that its trees were not cut or beaten. He would sit with me and talk to me, and I would feed him from the cucumbers and herbs. One day he said to me: 'I see that you do not leave this place.' I said: 'Indeed.' He said: 'I appoint you over what is here. Whoever you see cutting a tree or beating it, take his axe and his rope.' I said: 'Shall I take his cloak?' He said: 'No.'"

Most scholars hold that the game of the aforementioned protected pasture is not forbidden, because it is not a sanctuary (haram). It is rather a protected pasture which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reserved for horses and the camels of charity (zakat) and the poll tax (jizya) and the like.

It is disputed whether one who cuts a tree in the protected pasture owes compensation. Most hold that there is no liability for it. The more correct of the two views among the Shafiʿis is that compensation is obligatory for it, by its value, and that the one who cuts it is not stripped of his belongings. The value is spent on the purposes of the zakat livestock and the jizya.

* *

The thirteenth issue: Know that the majority of scholars hold that cutting the trees of the valley of Wajj and hunting its game is permitted. Al-Shafiʿi, may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him, said: "I dislike hunting in Wajj." His scholarly followers interpreted this as reprehensible in the sense of disapproval (karahat al-tahrim, i.e., near-prohibition).

(p. 458) They differed, on the view that it is forbidden, as to whether there is a penalty for it like the sanctuary of Madinah, or nothing is due, but the killer is to be disciplined. Most Shafiʿis hold the latter.

The evidence of those who hold that the game of Wajj is forbidden is what Abu Dawud, Ahmad, and al-Bukhari in his Tarikh related from al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwam (may Allah be pleased with him): that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The game of Wajj is forbidden," and the hadith continues.

Ibn Hajar said in al-Talkhis: Abu Dawud was silent about it, and al-Mundhiri graded it good (hasan), and ʿAbd al-Haqq was silent about it. Ibn al-Qattan criticized this, citing from al-Bukhari that it is not authentic (lam yasihha), and al-Azdi said likewise.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 96 (part 7 of 7):

Al-Dhahabi mentioned that al-Shafi'i authenticated it (ṣaḥḥaḥahu), and al-Khallal mentioned that Ahmad (ibn Hanbal) weakened it (ḍaʿʿafahu). Ibn Hibban said, regarding the narration of the one who transmitted it alone, who is Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Insan al-Ta'ifi, that he used to make mistakes (kāna yukhṭi'u). What this implies is the weakening of the hadith, since he has no other narration for it. If he erred in it, then it is weak. Al-Uqayli said: "It is not followed except through a channel close to it in weakness." Al-Nawawi said in *Sharh al-Muhadhdhab*: "Its chain (isnad) is weak."

Al-Bukhari mentioned in his *Tarikh* (*al-Tarikh al-Kabir*), in the biography of Abd Allah ibn Insan, that it is not authentic (lā yaṣiḥḥu).

Ibn Hajar said in *al-Taqrib* regarding the aforementioned Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Insan al-Thaqafi al-Ta'ifi: "Layyin al-hadith (weak in narration)." Likewise his father Abd Allah, who is his shaykh in this hadith, Ibn Hajar also said of him: "Layyin al-hadith."

Ibn Qudamah said in *al-Mughni*, regarding this hadith on the hunting of Wajj: "Ahmad weakened it, as mentioned by al-Khallal in *Kitab al-ʿIlal* (the Book of Defects)."

When you know this, it becomes clear to you that the argument of the majority (al-Jumhur) for the permissibility of hunting in Wajj and cutting its trees is that the hadith has not been established, and the original state is the freedom of the obligation (barā'at al-dhimmah). *Wajj*, with a fatḥah on the wāw and a shaddah on the jīm, is a land in al-Ta'if. Some scholars said it is a valley in the desert of al-Ta'if, and the intended meaning is not the town of al-Ta'if itself. It was said that it is the whole land of al-Ta'if, and it was said that it is the name of the fortresses of al-Ta'if, or of one of them. Wajj as mentioned may be confused with *Wahh* with an unpointed ḥā', which is a region of Nu'man.

When you know the ruling on hunting for the muhrim (one in the state of iḥrām), and the ruling on hunting in Makkah and Madinah and Wajj, from what we have mentioned, then know that a forbidden game animal (al-ṣayd al-muḥarram), if some of its legs are in the ḥill (the area outside the sacred precinct) and some of them in the ḥaram (the sacred precinct), or if it is on a branch extending into the ḥill while the root of its tree is in the ḥaram, then hunting it is forbidden with certainty, giving predominance (taghlīban) to the side of the sanctity of the ḥaram in both cases.

As for when the root of the tree is in the ḥill and its branches extend into the ḥaram, and one hunts a bird perched on the branches extending into the ḥaram, there is no doubt that it is hunted in the ḥaram, because the bird is in the air of the ḥaram.

Know that what some of the Hanafiyyah claimed, that the hadiths defining the ḥaram of Madinah are *mudtarib* (confused and contradictory), because in some narrations it occurs as *al-labatayn*, in some as *al-ḥarratayn*, in some as *al-jabalayn*, in some as *al-ma'zimayn*, and in some as ʿAyr and Thawr, is incorrect, because the reconciliation (al-jam') is evident with complete clarity. *Al-labatān* are the two well-known *ḥarrahs* (lava fields), which are black stones on the sides of Madinah. The two mountains are *al-ma'zimān*, which are ʿAyr and Thawr, and Madinah lies between the two ḥarrahs, just as it also lies between Thawr and ʿAyr, as anyone who looks at it can see. Thawr is a small reddish hill, rounded, behind Uhud on the north side.

Whoever among the scholars claims that there is no mountain called Thawr in Madinah has made an error, because it is known among people to this day, and it is also established in the authentic hadith.

Know that according to the reading of the Kufans, *fa-jazāʾun mithlu* (in the verse), with tanwin on *jazāʾun* and raf' on *mithlu*, the matter is clear. According to the reading of the majority, *fa-jazāʾu mithli* with the iḍāfah (genitive construction), the strongest of the opinions is that the iḍāfah is *bayāniyyah* (explanatory), meaning: a penalty which is the equivalent of what he killed of the cattle (al-naʿam), so its meaning returns to the first (statement). And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 105 (part 1 of 2):

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is [responsibility for] yourselves; no one who is astray can harm you once you are [rightly] guided﴾. The ignorant person may imagine from the apparent meaning of this noble verse that enjoining good and forbidding evil (al-amr bil-ma'ruf wal-nahy 'an al-munkar) is not obligatory. But the verse itself contains an indication that this applies when one has exerted his utmost effort and the one commanded has not accepted from him, and that is in His saying: ﴿once you are [rightly] guided﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 105]; for whoever abandons enjoining good has not been guided. Among those who said this were Hudhayfah and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, as al-Alusi transmitted from them in his Tafsir, and Ibn Jarir. Al-Qurtubi transmitted it from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam, and Ibn Jarir transmitted something similar from a group of the Companions, among them Ibn 'Umar and Ibn Mas'ud.

Some scholars said: ﴿once you are [rightly] guided﴾ means: you have commanded, but it was not heeded from you. Others said: enjoining good enters into what is meant by "being guided" in the verse, and this is very evident, and one who is fair should not deviate from it. (p-460)

Among what indicates that the one who abandons enjoining good is not guided is that God, may He be exalted, swore that man is in loss, in His saying: ﴿By time. Indeed, mankind is in loss, except for those who have believed and done righteous deeds and advised each other to truth and advised each other to patience﴾ [al-'Asr: 1, 2, 3]. So the truth is the obligation of enjoining good and forbidding evil, and after fulfilling the obligation, the straying of one who strays does not harm the one who commands. The verses have indicated this, such as His saying: ﴿And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively﴾ [al-Anfal: 25], and the hadiths indicate that if people do not enjoin good and do not forbid evil, God will overtake them all with a punishment from Him.

Among that is what the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded in their Sahihs, from the Mother of the Believers Umm al-Hakam Zaynab bint Jahsh, may Allah be pleased with her: that the Prophet ﷺ entered upon her in alarm and fright, saying: "There is no god but Allah! Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near. Today there has been opened from the barrier of Gog and Magog such as this," and he made a circle with his two fingers, the thumb and the one next to it. I said: "O Messenger of Allah! Will we be destroyed while the righteous are among us?" He said: "Yes, when wickedness increases."

And from an-Nu'man ibn Bashir, may Allah be pleased with both of them, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "The example of one who stands within the limits of Allah and one who falls into them is like a people who drew lots over a ship, so some of them were at its top and some at its bottom. Those at its bottom, when they needed water, passed by those above them, and they said: 'If only we made a hole in our share and did not harm those above us.' If they leave them and what they want, they will all perish; and if they take hold of their hands, they will be saved and all be saved." Recorded by al-Bukhari and at-Tirmidhi.

And from Abu Bakr as-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "O people, you recite this verse: ﴿O you who have believed, upon you is [responsibility for] yourselves; no one who is astray can harm you once you are [rightly] guided﴾, and I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: 'If people see the wrongdoer and do not take hold of his hand, Allah is about to overtake them all with a punishment from Him.'" Narrated by Abu Dawud, at-Tirmidhi, and an-Nasa'i with sound chains.

And from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The first thing that entered deficiency upon the Children of Israel was that a man would meet another man and say: 'O such-and-such, fear Allah and leave off what you are doing, for it is not lawful for you.' Then he would meet him the next day and he would still be in his state, yet that would not prevent him from being his companion at table, his drinking partner, and his companion at sitting. When they did that, Allah struck their hearts, some against others." Then he recited: ﴿Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed upon the tongue of David and Jesus, the son of Mary, because they disobeyed and were transgressing﴾ ﴿They used not to forbid one another from wrongdoing which they committed. Wretched was what they used to do﴾ ﴿You see many of them allying themselves with those who disbelieve. Wretched is what their souls have put forth for them, that Allah has become angry at them, and in punishment they will abide eternally﴾ ﴿And if they had believed in Allah, and the Prophet, and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies; but many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 79, 80, 81]. Then he said: "No! By Allah, you will enjoin good, you will forbid evil, you will take hold of the hand of the wrongdoer, you will turn him toward the truth in full turning, and you will confine him to the truth in full confinement; or Allah will strike your hearts, some against others, and then He will curse you as He cursed them."

Recorded by Abu Dawud and at-Tirmidhi, who said: hasan. This is the wording of Abu Dawud. The wording of at-Tirmidhi: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When the Children of Israel fell into sins, their scholars forbade them, but they did not desist, so they sat with them, ate with them, and drank with them; so Allah struck their hearts, some against others, and cursed them upon the tongue of David and Jesus, the son of Mary, because they disobeyed and were transgressing." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sat up, having been reclining, and said: "No, by Him in whose hand is my soul, until you turn them toward the truth in full turning."

The meaning of "turn them" (ta'tiruhum) is: incline them, and the meaning of "confine him" (taqsurunahu) is: restrain him. The hadiths on this subject are very numerous, and in them is clear evidence that enjoining good and forbidding evil enters into His saying: ﴿once you are [rightly] guided﴾. It is supported by the abundance of verses that indicate the obligation of enjoining good and forbidding evil:

• such as His saying: ﴿And let there be [arising] from you a nation inviting to good, enjoining what is right, and forbidding what is wrong; and those are the successful﴾ [Al 'Imran: 104],
• and His saying: ﴿You are the best nation produced for mankind; you enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong﴾ [Al 'Imran: 110],
• and His saying: ﴿Those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel were cursed upon the tongue of David and Jesus, the son of Mary, because they disobeyed and were transgressing﴾ ﴿They used not to forbid one another from wrongdoing which they committed. Wretched was what they used to do﴾,
• and His saying: ﴿And say, "The truth is from your Lord, so whoever wills let him believe, and whoever wills let him disbelieve"﴾ [al-Kahf: 29],
• and His saying: ﴿So declare what you are commanded﴾ [al-Hijr: 94],
• and His saying: ﴿We saved those who forbade evil and seized those who wronged with a grievous punishment for their defiant disobedience﴾ [al-A'raf: 165],
• and His saying: ﴿And fear a trial which will not strike those who have wronged among you exclusively﴾ [al-Anfal: 25].

The verification of its meaning: the trial that encompasses the wrongdoer and others is that when people see wrongdoing and do not change it, God overtakes them all with punishment, the righteous and the wicked among them; and a group of the people of knowledge explained it this way, and the sound hadiths bear witness to it, as we have already mentioned some of them.

* *

Issues related to enjoining good and forbidding evil:

The first issue: Know that each of the one who commands and the one who is commanded is obligated to follow the truth being commanded. The sound Sunnah has indicated that whoever commands good and does not do it, and forbids evil and does it, is a donkey of the donkeys of Hell, dragging his intestines in it.

The Mighty Qur'an has indicated that the one commanded who turns away from the reminder is also a donkey. As for the Sunnah mentioned, it is his saying ﷺ: "A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and thrown into the Fire, and his entrails will spill out, and he will go around with them in the Fire as a donkey goes around its millstone. The people of the Fire will gather around him and say: 'O so-and-so, what has happened to you? Did you not used to command us to do good and forbid us from evil?' He will say: 'I used to command you to do good and not do it myself, and I used to forbid you from evil and do it myself.'" Recorded by al-Bukhari and Muslim in their Sahihs from the hadith of Usamah ibn Zayd, may Allah be pleased with both of them.

The meaning of "his entrails spill out" (tandaliqu aqtabuhu) is: his intestines hang down. May Allah protect us and the Muslims from every evil.

And from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "On the night I was taken on the Night Journey, I saw men whose lips were being cut with scissors of fire; every time they were cut, they returned. I said to Gabriel: 'Who are these?' He said: 'These are preachers from your Ummah who used to command people to righteousness and forget themselves, while they recite the Book. Do they not reason?'" Recorded by Imam Ahmad, Ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Bazzar, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilyah, Ibn Hibban, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi, as ash-Shawkani and others transmitted from them.

And from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them: "A man came to him and said: 'O Ibn 'Abbas, I want to command good and forbid evil.' Ibn 'Abbas said: 'Have you attained that?' He said: 'I hope so.' He said: 'If you do not fear being exposed by three letters in the Book of Allah, then do it.' He said: 'And what are they?' He said: 'His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Do you order the people to righteousness and forget yourselves?﴾ and the verse [al-Baqarah: 44]; His saying: ﴿Great is hatred in the sight of Allah that you say what you do not do﴾ [al-Saff: 3]; and His saying about the righteous servant Shu'ayb, upon him and upon our Prophet be prayer and peace: ﴿And I do not intend to contradict you in that which I forbid you﴾ [Hud: 88]." Recorded by al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn 'Asakir, as ash-Shawkani and others also transmitted from them.

Know that the truth is that this severe threat we mentioned, of entrails spilling out in the Fire and lips being cut with scissors of fire, is not for enjoining good, but for committing evil knowingly while advising people against it. So the truth is that the obligation of enjoining good does not fall from the righteous or the wicked, and the threat is for disobedience, not for enjoining good, since in itself it contains nothing but good. Well has said the one who said [al-Kamil]:

"Do not forbid a trait while you yourself display its like; it is a great shame upon you when you do it."

And another said [al-Tawil]:

"An impious person who commands people to piety is a physician who treats people while he is sick."

And another said [al-Tawil]:

"For if you do not do what you command, you will be destroyed by the one you command, doing it."

As for the verse indicating that the one who turns away from reminder is also like a donkey, it is His saying: ﴿So what is [the matter] with them that they are turning away from the reminder? As if they were startled donkeys fleeing from a lion﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 49, 50, 51]. The lesson is in the generality of the wording, not the specificity of the causes. So it is obligatory on the one who reminds, and on the one who is reminded, to act according to the requirement of the reminder, and to guard against heedlessness toward it, lest they become two donkeys of the donkeys of Hell.

* *

Second issue: a person who commands the good must have knowledge, by which he knows that what he commands is good and what he forbids is evil; for if he is ignorant of this, he may command what is not good and forbid what is not evil, especially in this age in which ignorance has spread and truth has become reprehensible and reprehensible things have become good. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Say: This is my way; I call to Allah with insight, I and whoever follows me﴾ [Yusuf: 108]. This shows that the caller to Allah must be upon insight, which is the clear proof with which there is no confusion regarding the truth. His call to Allah should be with wisdom, good manner and gentleness along with clarifying the truth, due to the saying of Allah the Exalted: (p-464) ﴿Call to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good admonition﴾ [al-Nahl: 125]. If his call to Allah is with harshness, violence and roughness, it harms more than it benefits. Therefore, commanding the good should not be ascribed absolutely except to one who combines knowledge, wisdom, and patience over the harm of people, because commanding the good is the duty of the messengers and their followers, and it necessarily entails harm from people, since they are naturally inclined to oppose whoever confronts their corrupt desires and false aims. For this reason the righteous servant Luqman the Wise said to his son, as Allah related of him: ﴿And enjoin what is good, forbid what is evil, and be patient over what afflicts you﴾ [Luqman: 17]. When the Prophet ﷺ said to Waraqah ibn Nawfal: "Will they expel me?" meaning the Quraysh, Waraqah informed him that no one had brought this religion except that he was opposed, and it was narrated from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "The truth has not left Umar a friend." Know that a matter is not judged to be evil unless there is a proof for that from the Book of Allah the Exalted, or the Sunnah of His Prophet ﷺ, or the consensus of the Muslims.
As for matters of ijtihad where there is no explicit text, one of the mujtahids who differ is not judged to be committing an evil; the one who is correct among them is rewarded for his correctness, and the one who errs among them is excused, as is known in its place.
Know that the call to Allah is by two ways: a way of gentleness and a way of harshness. As for the way of gentleness, it is calling to Allah with wisdom and good admonition, and clarifying the proofs in the best and gentlest manner. If this way succeeds, then well and good, and that is what is sought. If it does not succeed, the way of harshness becomes necessary, by the sword, until Allah alone is worshipped, His limits are established, His commands are obeyed, and His prohibitions are avoided. To this there is an allusion in the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿We certainly sent Our messengers with clear proofs and sent down with them the Book and the Balance that people may uphold justice. And We sent down iron, in which is great might﴾ [al-Hadid: 25].
In it is an indication to the use of the sword after establishing the proof. If the books do not benefit, then the battalions become necessary, and Allah the Exalted restrains by the authority what He does not restrain by the Qur'an.
* *
Third issue: it is a condition for the permissibility of commanding the good that it not lead to a greater corruption than that evil, due to the consensus of the Muslims on committing the lesser of two harms. In "Maraqi al-Su'ud" he said, in rajaz meter:
"And commit the lighter of two harms, and choose when the two are equal."
And it is a condition for its obligation that there be a presumption of benefit from it. If one is certain that there is no benefit in it, it is not obligatory upon him, as the apparent meaning of the saying of Allah the Exalted indicates: ﴿So remind, if the reminder benefits﴾ [al-A'la: 9], and the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Rather, enjoin one another to good and forbid one another from evil, until you see avarice obeyed, desire followed, the world preferred, and every person of opinion pleased with his own opinion; then upon you is your own self, and leave aside the affair of the common people, for behind you are days in which the patient one is like one who grasps a live coal; for the one who acts in them there is the reward of fifty men who do the same as your deeds." In another wording: "It was said: O Messenger of Allah, the reward of fifty men from us, or from them? He said: Rather, the reward of fifty from you." Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, al-Hakim, who authenticated it, Abu Dawud, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, al-Baghawi in his "Mu'jam," Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Abu al-Shaykh, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in "al-Shu'ab," from the hadith of Abu Tha'labah al-Khushani, may Allah be pleased with him. The narrator said: This hadith was narrated by Abu Umayyah al-Sha'bani, who asked him about the saying of Allah: ﴿Upon you is your own self﴾, and he said: By Allah, I asked about it one who is informed; I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he said: "Rather, enjoin," to the end of the hadith.
The attributes mentioned in the hadith, of obeyed avarice, followed desire, etc., are a presumption of the non-benefit of commanding the good; so the hadith indicates that if its benefit is absent, its obligation falls.
Admonition
Commanding the good has three wisdoms:
The first: establishing the proof of Allah over His creation, as He the Exalted said: ﴿Messengers as bearers of good news and warners, so that people will have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [al-Nisa: 165].
The second: the commander's release from the burden of the obligation of commanding the good, as Allah the Exalted said about the righteous of the people among whom some had transgressed on the Sabbath: ﴿They said: as an excuse to your Lord﴾ [al-A'raf: 164], and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So turn away from them, for you are not blameworthy﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 54]. This shows that if he were not released from the burden, he would be blameworthy.
The third: hope of benefit for the one commanded, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿An excuse to your Lord, and perhaps they will fear Him﴾ (p-466) and Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And remind, for the reminder benefits the believers﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 55]. We have clarified this discussion in our book "Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab" in Surah al-A'la, in the discussion of the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So remind, if the reminder benefits﴾ [al-A'la: 9]. A person must command his family with good, such as his wife, his children, and the like, and forbid them from evil, due to the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire﴾ [al-Tahrim: 6], and the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: "Each of you is a shepherd and each of you is responsible for his flock," the hadith.
* *
Fourth issue: know that among the greatest kinds of commanding the good is a word of truth before an unjust ruler. From Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The best jihad is a word of justice before an unjust ruler." Narrated by Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi, who said: a hasan hadith.
And from Tariq ibn Shihab, may Allah be pleased with him: "A man asked the Prophet ﷺ while he had placed his foot in the stirrup: Which jihad is best? He said: A word of truth before an unjust ruler." Narrated by al-Nasa'i with a sahih chain.
As al-Nawawi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Know that the sound hadith has clarified that the states of the subjects with a ruler who commits what is not proper are three:
The first: that one is able to advise him and command him with good and forbid him from evil, without there resulting from him a harm greater than the first. The one who commands him in this state is a mujahid, safe from sin even if his advice does not benefit; and his advice must be with good admonition and gentleness, for that is the presumption of benefit.
The second: that one is not able to advise him, due to his lashing out at the one who commands him, or because conveying his advice leads to a greater evil. In this state the denunciation is in the heart, by disliking his evil and being displeased with it, and this state is the weakest of faith.
The third: that one is pleased with the evil that the ruler does and follows him in it; this one is his partner in sin. The hadith mentioned is what we presented in Surah al-Baqarah from the Mother of the Believers Umm Salamah Hind bint Abi Umayyah, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "There will be rulers over you, and you will recognize and deny; whoever disliked has been cleared, and whoever denounced has been safe, but whoever was pleased and followed..." They said: "(p-467) O Messenger of Allah, should we not fight them?" He said: "No, as long as they establish the prayer among you." Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih.
So his saying ﷺ "whoever disliked" means with his heart, and he was not able to denounce with hand or tongue; "has been cleared" of sin and has discharged his duty; "whoever denounced" according to his capacity "has been safe" from this disobedience; "whoever was pleased" with it "and followed" in it, he is a disobedient one like its doer.
Its parallel is the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, in Muslim: he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; if he is not able, then with his tongue; if he is not able, then with his heart, and that is the weakest of faith." And his saying in this noble verse: ﴿Upon you is your own self﴾ is an imperative of urging, meaning: keep to guarding it, as he indicated in the "Khulasah" with his saying:
"The verb among its names is 'alaykum, and likewise 'duunaka' with 'ilaykum."

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 106:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And we will not conceal the testimony of Allah, for then we would be among the sinners﴾. In this noble verse He mentioned that one who conceals testimony is sinful, and He explained in another place that this sin is one of the sins of the heart, namely His statement: ﴿And whoever conceals it, his heart is sinful﴾ [al-Baqarah: 283]. It is well known that the source of all sins and acts of obedience is the heart; for when it is sound, the whole body is sound, and when it is corrupt, the whole body is corrupt.

⁕ ⁕ ⁕

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿Or two others from other than you﴾, the verse.

This verse indicates the acceptance of the testimony of disbelievers regarding bequest during travel, and other verses have come that indicate the opposite of that, such as His statement: ﴿Only those who do not believe in the signs of Allah fabricate lies, and those are the liars﴾ [al-Nahl: 105].

And His statement: ﴿And do not accept their testimony ever, and those are the defiantly disobedient﴾ [al-Nur: 4], meaning that disbelievers are more deserving of having their testimony rejected.

And His statement: ﴿And call to witness two just men from among you﴾ [al-Talaq: 2].

And His statement: ﴿And call to witness two witnesses from among your men. But if they are not two men, then a man and two women from those whom you accept as witnesses﴾, the verse [al-Baqarah: 282].

The answer to this, according to the view of those who do not accept the testimony of disbelievers regarding bequest during travel, is that they say: His statement ﴿or two others from other than you﴾ is abrogated by the verses requiring justice (al-'adalah) as a condition. Whereas those who say their testimony is accepted say it is a muhkam (definitive, non-abrogated) verse that specifies the generality of other verses. This disagreement is well known, and the way of answering according to both views is clear.

As for the view of those who said that the meaning of His statement ﴿two just men from among you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 95] is from the tribe of the one making the bequest, and His statement ﴿or two others from other than you﴾ means from other than the tribe of the one making the bequest, from among the rest of the Muslims, then there is no difficulty in the verse.

However, the majority of scholars hold that His statement ﴿from other than you﴾ means from other than the Muslims, and that His statement "from among you" means from among the Muslims. Accordingly, the answer is what has preceded, and Allah knows best.

The author said in (Dispelling the Appearance of Contradiction from the Verses of the Book):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day when Allah will gather the Messengers and say, "What was the response you received?" They will say, "We have no knowledge. Indeed, You, You are the Knower of the unseen."﴾

(p-275) From this verse it may be understood that the Messengers will not bear witness on the Day of Resurrection concerning their nations.

Other verses have come that indicate they will bear witness concerning their nations, such as His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness and bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness against these?﴾ [An-Nisa' 4:41].

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [mention] the Day We will raise up in every nation a witness against them from among themselves, and We will bring you as a witness against these.﴾ [An-Nahl 16:89].

The answer has three aspects:

The first, which is the view chosen by Ibn Jarir, and of which Ibn Kathir said: "There is no doubt that it is good," is that the meaning of ﴿We have no knowledge﴾ is: except for knowledge that You know better than we do. So we have no knowledge in comparison to Your all-encompassing knowledge of everything. Although we know who answered us, we know only the outward appearances and have no knowledge of the inward realities, whereas You are the One who is aware of the secrets and what the hearts conceal. Thus our knowledge, in comparison to Your knowledge, is as no knowledge.

The second, which was also the view of Mujahid, as-Suddi and al-Hasan al-Basri, as Ibn Kathir and others transmitted from them, is that they said: ﴿We have no knowledge﴾ because of the severity of the terror of the Day of Resurrection that overcame them. Then that state passed from them, and they bore witness concerning their nations.

The third, which is the weakest of them, is that the meaning of His saying ﴿What was the response you received?﴾ is: "What did they do after you, and what innovations did they introduce after you?" ﴿They will say, "We have no knowledge."﴾ Ibn Kathir and others mentioned this view, but its remoteness from the apparent meaning of the Qur'an is not hidden.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when you bring forth the dead by My permission﴾. Its meaning is their bringing out from their graves alive, by the will and power of Allah, as He clarified it in His saying: ﴿And I heal the blind and the leper, and I bring the dead to life by the permission of Allah﴾ [Al 'Imran: 49].

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when I restrained the Children of Israel from you when you came to them with clear proofs﴾, the verse. He did not mention here the manner of their being restrained from him, but He explained it in other places, such as:

• His saying: ﴿And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him, but it was made to appear so to them﴾,

• and His saying: ﴿And they did not kill him with certainty. Rather, Allah raised him to Himself﴾ [An-Nisa: 158],

• and His saying: ﴿and purifying you from those who disbelieve﴾ [Al 'Imran: 55],

and other verses.

In the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And when I inspired the disciples﴾ — the verse [and so on]. Some scholars of knowledge said: What is meant by the inspiration (al-iyhaa') to the disciples (al-Hawariyyun) is inspiration in the sense of divine inspiration (al-ilham). What supports this is that the word inspiration (al-iyhaa') occurs in the Qur'an with the meaning of ilham, as in His saying: ﴿And your Lord inspired the bee﴾ — the verse [An-Nahl: 68], meaning He inspired it. Some scholars said: And from this is ﴿And We inspired the mother of Musa, saying: Suckle him﴾ [Al-Qasas: 7]. Other scholars said its meaning is: I inspired the disciples with a true (haqiqi) inspiration through the medium of Isa — upon him and upon our Prophet be prayers and peace.

Commentary of al-Shinqiti (Adwa' al-Bayan) on surah 5, verse 115:

The author said in (Daf' Iham al-Idtirab 'an Ayat al-Kitab):

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah said, "Indeed, I will send it down to you. But whoever disbelieves afterward among you - indeed, I will punish him with a punishment by which I will not punish anyone among the worlds."﴾

This noble verse indicates that the most severe of people in punishment on the Day of Resurrection is one who disbelieved from among the companions of the table (al-Ma'idah).

Some other verses contain what gives the impression of the opposite, such as His saying: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest level of the Fire﴾ [an-Nisa': 145], and His saying: ﴿And on the Day the Hour appears, [it will be said], "Admit the people of Pharaoh into the severest punishment."﴾ [Ghafir: 46].

The answer is that there is no contradiction between the verse "Admit the people of Pharaoh" and the verse "Indeed, the hypocrites," because each of the people of Pharaoh and the hypocrites is in the lowest levels of the Fire, in the most severe punishment, and there is nothing in the two verses that indicates that some of them are more severely punished than the others.

As for His saying, "for indeed I will punish him" (the verse), it is answered in two ways:

The first, which is what Ibn Kathir said: the intended meaning of "the worlds" is the worlds of their time, and according to this there is no problem. A parallel to this is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And that I preferred you over the worlds﴾ [al-Baqarah: 47], as has previously been mentioned.

The second is what some have said: that what is intended is the worldly punishment, which is their transformation into pigs. But what indicates that it refers to the punishment of the Hereafter is what Ibn Jarir narrated from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: "The most severe of people in punishment on the Day of Resurrection are three: the hypocrites, those among the companions of the table who disbelieved, and the people of Pharaoh."

This problem concerning the companions of the table arises only according to the view that the table was sent down and that some of them disbelieved after its descent. As for the view of al-Hasan and Mujahid, that they feared the threat and said, "We have no need for its descent," so it was not sent down, then there is no problem.

However, the apparent meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, I will send it down﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 115] contradicts that. And according to the view that it was sent down, the problem arises only if it is established that some of them disbelieved, as is not hidden.
